flags.name: undefok

flags.description: If non-empty, HandleCommandLineCompletions() will hijack the process and attempt to do bash-style command line flag completion on this value.

flags.name: helpshort

flags.name: helpxml

flags.name: version
flags.description: show version and build info and exit

flags.name: catalog_max_lock_skipped_topic_updates
flags.description: Maximum number of topic updates skipped for a table due to lock contention in catalogd after which it mustbe added to the topic the update log. This limit only applies to distinct lock operations which block the topic update thread.

flags.name: catalog_operation_log_size
flags.description: Number of catalog operation log records to retain in catalogd. If -1, the operation log has unbounded size.

flags.name: catalog_service_port
flags.description: port where the CatalogService is running

flags.name: catalog_topic_mode
flags.description:
The type of data that the catalog service will publish into the Catalog StateStore topic. Valid values are 'full', 'mixed', or 'minimal'.

In 'full' mode, complete catalog objects are published any time a new version is available. In 'minimal' mode, only a minimal object is published when a new version of a catalog object is available. In 'mixed' mode, both types of topic entries are published.

When all impalad coordinators are configured with --use_local_catalog disabled (the default), 'full' mode should be used. If all impalad coordinators are configured with --use_local_catalog enabled, 'minimal' mode should be used. When some impalads are configured with --use_local_catalog disabled and others configured with it enabled, then 'mixed' mode is required.

flags.name: common_hms_event_types
flags.description: Common HMS event types that will be used in eventTypeSkipList when fetching events from HMS. The strings come from constants in org.apache.hadoop.hive.metastore.messaging.MessageBuilder. When bumping Hive versions, the list might need to be updated accordingly. To avoid bringing too much computation overhead to HMS's underlying RDBMS in evaluating predicates of EVENT_TYPE != 'xxx', rare event types are not tracked in this list. They are CREATE_FUNCTION,DROP_FUNCTION,ADD_PRIMARYKEY,ADD_FOREIGNKEY,ADD_UNIQUECONSTRAINT,ADD_NOTNULLCONSTRAINT, ADD_DEFAULTCONSTRAINT, ADD_CHECKCONSTRAINT, DROP_CONSTRAINT,CREATE_ISCHEMA, ALTER_ISCHEMA, DROP_ISCHEMA, ADD_SCHEMA_VERSION,ALTER_SCHEMA_VERSION, DROP_SCHEMA_VERSION, CREATE_CATALOG, ALTER_CATALOG,DROP_CATALOG, CREATE_DATACONNECTOR, ALTER_DATACONNECTOR, DROP_DATACONNECTOR.

flags.name: default_skipped_hms_event_types
flags.description: HMS event types that are not used by Impala. They are skipped by default in fetching HMS event batches. Only in few places they will be fetched, e.g. fetching the latest event time in HMS.

flags.name: enable_reload_events
flags.description: This configuration is used to fire a refresh/invalidate table event to the HMS such that other event processors (such as other Impala catalogds) that poll HMS notification logs can process this event. The default value is false, so impala will not fire this event. If enabled, impala will fire this event and other catalogD will process it.This config only affects the firing of the reload event. Processing of reload event will always happen

flags.name: enable_skipping_older_events
flags.description: This configuration is used to skip anyolder events in the event processor based on the lastRefreshEventId on thedatabase/table/partition in the cache. All the DML queries that change the metadatain the catalogD's cache will update the lastRefreshEventId i.e.., fetch the latestavailable event on HMS and set it on the object. In case the event processor islagging, the older events in event processor queue can be skipped by comparing thecurrent event id to that of lastRefreshEventId. The default is set to false todisable the optimisation. Set this true to enable skipping the older events andquickly catch with the events of HMS

flags.name: enable_sync_to_latest_event_on_ddls
flags.description: This configuration is used to sync db/table in catalogd cache to latest HMS event id whenever DDL operations are performed from Impala shell and catalog metastore server (if enabled). If this config is enabled, then the flag invalidate_hms_cache_on_ddls should be disabled

flags.name: fallback_to_hms_on_errors
flags.description: This configuration is only used if start_hms_server is true. This is used to determine if the Catalog should fallback to the backing HMS service if there are errors while processing the HMS request

flags.name: file_metadata_reload_properties
flags.description: This configuration is used to whitelist the table properties that are supposed torefresh file metadata when these properties are changed. To skip this optimization,set the value to empty string

flags.name: hms_event_incremental_refresh_transactional_table
flags.description: When set to true events processor will refresh transactional tables incrementally for partition level events. Otherwise, it will always reload the whole table for transactional tables.

flags.name: hms_port
flags.description: If start_hms_server is set to true, this configuration specifies the port number at which it is started.

flags.name: invalidate_global_metadata_on_event_processing_failure
flags.description: This configuration is used to global invalidate metadata when invalidate_metadata_on_event_processing_failure cannot invalidate metadata for table(s). The default value is false. When enabled, global invalidate metadata is performed automatically. Otherwise, failure can put metastore event processor in non-active state.

flags.name: invalidate_hms_cache_on_ddls
flags.description: This configuration is used only if start_hms_server is true. This is used to invalidate catalogd cache for non transactional tables if alter/create/delete table hms apis are invoked over catalogd's metastore endpoint

flags.name: invalidate_metadata_on_event_processing_failure
flags.description: This configuration is used to invalidate metadata for table(s) upon event process failure other than HMS connection issues. The default value is true. When enabled, invalidate metadata is performed automatically upon event process failure. Otherwise, failure can put metastore event processor in non-active state.

flags.name: max_wait_time_for_sync_ddl_s
flags.description: Maximum time (in seconds) until which a sync ddl operation will wait for the updated tables to be the added to the catalog topic. A value of 0 means sync ddl operation will wait as long as necessary until the update is propogated to all the coordinators. This flag only takes effect when topic_update_tbl_max_wait_time_ms is enabled.A value greater than 0 means catalogd will wait until that number of seconds before throwing an error indicating that not all the coordinators might have applied the changes caused due to the ddl.

flags.name: start_hms_server
flags.description: When set to true catalog server starts a HMS server at a port specified by hms_port flag

flags.name: topic_update_log_gc_frequency
flags.description: Frequency at which the entries of the catalog topic update log are garbage collected. An entry may survive for (2 * TOPIC_UPDATE_LOG_GC_FREQUENCY) - 1 topic updates.

flags.name: topic_update_tbl_max_wait_time_ms
flags.description: Maximum time (in milliseconds) catalog's topic update thread will wait to acquire lock on table. If the topic update thread cannot acquire a table lock it skips the table from that topic update and processes the table in the next update. However to prevent starvation it only skips the table catalog_max_lock_skipped_topic_updates many times. After that limit is hit, topic thread block until it acquires the table lock. A value of 0 disables the timeout based locking which means topic update thread will always block until table lock is acquired.

flags.name: enable_reading_puffin_stats
flags.description: Impala will only read Iceberg Puffin stats files if this flag is set to true.

flags.name: initial_hms_cnxn_timeout_s
flags.description: Number of seconds catalogd will wait to establish an initial connection to the HMS before exiting.

flags.name: load_catalog_in_background
flags.description: If true, loads catalog metadata in the background. If false, metadata is loaded lazily (on access).

flags.name: max_hdfs_partitions_parallel_load
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of threads used to load block metadata for HDFS based partitioned tables. Due to HDFS architectural limitations, it is unlikely to get a linear speed up beyond 5 threads.

flags.name: max_nonhdfs_partitions_parallel_load
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of threads used to load block metadata for tables that do not support the notion of blocks/storage IDs. Currently supported for S3/ADLS.

flags.name: num_metadata_loading_threads
flags.description: (Advanced) The number of metadata loading threads (degree of parallelism) to use when loading catalog metadata.

flags.name: asm_module_dir
flags.description: if set, saves disassembly for generated IR modules to the specified directory.

flags.name: disable_optimization_passes
flags.description: if true, disables llvm optimization passes (used for testing)

flags.name: dump_ir
flags.description: if true, output IR after optimization passes

flags.name: opt_module_dir
flags.description: if set, saves optimized generated IR modules to the specified directory.

flags.name: perf_map
flags.description: if true, generate /tmp/perf-<pid>.map file for linux perf symbols. This is not recommended for production use because it may affect performance.

flags.name: print_llvm_ir_instruction_count
flags.description: if true, prints the instruction counts of all JIT'd functions

flags.name: unopt_module_dir
flags.description: if set, saves unoptimized generated IR modules to the specified directory.

flags.name: abort_on_config_error
flags.description: Abort Impala startup if there are improper configs or running on unsupported hardware.

flags.name: active_catalogd_designation_monitoring_interval_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Interval (in ms) with which the statestore monitors if active catalogd is designated.

flags.name: anonymous_user_name
flags.description: Default username used when a client connects to an unsecured impala daemon and does not specify a username.

flags.name: be_principal
flags.description: Kerberos principal for backend network connections only,overriding --principal if set. Must not be set if --principal is not set.

flags.name: blacklisted_dbs
flags.description: Comma separated list for blacklisted databases. Configure which databases to be skipped for loading (in startup and global INVALIDATE METADATA). Users can't access, create, or drop databases which are blacklisted.

flags.name: blacklisted_tables
flags.description: Comma separated full names (in format: <db>.<table>) of blacklisted tables. Configure which tables to be skipped for loading (in startup and resetting metadata of the table). Users can't access, create, or drop tables which are blacklisted

flags.name: buffer_pool_clean_pages_limit
flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on bytes of clean pages that will be accumulated in the buffer pool. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the buffer pool limit ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given..

flags.name: buffer_pool_limit
flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on buffer pool size. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the process memory limit (minus the JVM heap if --mem_limit_includes_jvm is true) ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given. The default value and behaviour of this flag may change between releases.

flags.name: catalogd_ha_preemption_wait_period_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which statestore designates the first registered catalogd as active if statestore does not receive registration request from the second catalogd.

flags.name: compact_catalog_topic
flags.description: If true, catalog updates sent via the statestore are compacted before transmission. This saves network bandwidth at the cost of a small quantity of CPU time. Enable this option in cluster with large catalogs. It must be enabled on both the catalog service, and all Impala demons.

flags.name: debug_actions
flags.description: For testing only. Uses the same format as the debug action query options, but allows for injection of debug actions in code paths where query options are not available.

flags.name: disable_kudu
flags.description: If true, Kudu features will be disabled.

flags.name: enable_catalogd_ha
flags.description: Set to true to enable CatalogD HA

flags.name: enable_catalogd_hms_cache
flags.description: If true, response for the HMS APIs that are implemented in catalogd will be served from catalogd. If this flag is false or a given API is not implemented in catalogd, it will be redirected to HMS.

flags.name: enable_incremental_metadata_updates
flags.description: If true, Catalog Server will send incremental table updates in partition level in the statestore topic updates. Legacy coordinators will apply the partition updates incrementally, i.e. reuse unchanged partition metadata. Disable this feature by setting this to false in the Catalog Server. Then metadata of each table will be propagated as a whole object in the statestore topic updates. Note that legacy coordinators can apply incremental or full table updates so don't need this flag.

flags.name: enable_insert_events
flags.description: Enables insert events in the events processor. When this configuration is set to true Impala will generate INSERT event types which when received by other Impala clusters can be used to automatically refresh the tables or partitions. Event processing must be turned on for this flag to have any effect.

flags.name: enable_legacy_avx_support
flags.description: If true, Impala relaxes its x86_64 CPU feature requirement to allow running on machines with AVX but no AVX2. This allows running Impala on older machines without AVX2 support. This is a legacy mode that will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: enable_minidumps
flags.description: Whether to enable minidump generation upon process crash or SIGUSR1.

flags.name: enable_process_lifetime_heap_profiling
flags.description: (Advanced) Enables heap profiling for the lifetime of the process. Profile output will be stored in the directory specified by -heap_profile_dir. Enabling this option will disable the on-demand/remote server profile handlers.

flags.name: enable_stats_extrapolation
flags.description: If true, uses table statistics computed with COMPUTE STATS to extrapolate the row counts of partitions.

flags.name: force_catalogd_active
flags.description: Set to true to force this catalogd instance to take active role. It's used to perform manual fail over for catalog service.

flags.name: geospatial_library
flags.description: Specifies which implementation of geospatial functions should be included as builtins. Possible values: ["NONE", "HIVE_ESRI"]

flags.name: heap_profile_dir
flags.description: Output directory to store heap profiles. If not set profiles are stored in the current working directory.

flags.name: hms_event_polling_interval_s
flags.description: Configure catalogd to refresh cached table metadata based on metastore events. These metastore events could be generated by external systems like Apache Hive or a different Impala cluster using the same Hive metastore server as this one. A non-zero value of this flag sets the polling interval of catalogd in seconds to fetch new metastore events. A value of zero disables this feature. When enabled, this flag has the same effect as "REFRESH" statement on the table for certain metastore event types. Additionally, in case of events which detect creation or removal of objects from metastore, catalogd adds or removes such objects from its cached metadata. This feature is independent of time and memory based automatic invalidation of tables.

flags.name: hostname
flags.description: Hostname to use for this daemon, also used as part of the Kerberos principal, if enabled. If not set, the system default will be used

flags.name: iceberg_allow_datafiles_in_table_location_only
flags.description: If true, Impala does not allow Iceberg data file locations outside of the table directory during reads

flags.name: iceberg_always_allow_merge_on_read_operations
flags.description: Impala can only write delete files with 'merge-on-read'. If this flag is true, Impala allows executing DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE operations on Iceberg tables even if the table property is 'copy-on-write'.

flags.name: iceberg_reload_new_files_threshold
flags.description: (Advanced) If during a table refresh the number of new files are greater than this, catalogd will use a recursive file listing to load file metadata. If number of new files are less or equal to this, catalogd will load the file metadata one by one.

flags.name: impala_slow_rpc_threshold_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Threshold for considering Impala internal RPCs to be unusually slow. Slow RPCs trigger additional logging and other diagnostics. Lowering this value may result in false positivesThis overrides KRPC's --rpc_duration_too_long_ms setting.

flags.name: inc_stats_size_limit_bytes
flags.description: Maximum size of incremental stats the catalog is allowed to serialize per table. This limit is set as a safety check, to prevent the JVM from hitting a maximum array limit of 1GB (or OOM) while building the thrift objects to send to impalads. By default, it's set to 200MB

flags.name: invalidate_tables_on_memory_pressure
flags.description: Configure catalogd to invalidate recently unused tables when the old GC generation is almost full. This is independent from time-based invalidation configured by invalidate_table_timeout_s. To enable this feature, a true flag must be applied to both catalogd and impalad.

flags.name: invalidate_tables_timeout_s
flags.description: If a table has not been referenced in a SQL statement for more than the configured amount of time, the catalog server will automatically evict its cached metadata about this table. This has the same effect as a user-initiated "INVALIDATE METADATA" statement on the table. Configuring this to 0 disables time-based automatic invalidation of tables. This is independent from memory-based invalidation configured by invalidate_tables_on_memory_pressure. To enable this feature, a non-zero flag must be applied to both catalogd and impalad.

flags.name: keytab_file
flags.description: Absolute path to Kerberos keytab file

flags.name: krb5_ccname
flags.description: Absolute path to the file based credentials cache that we pass to the KRB5CCNAME environment variable.

flags.name: krb5_conf
flags.description: Absolute path to Kerberos krb5.conf if in a non-standard location. Does not normally need to be set.

flags.name: krb5_debug_file
flags.description: Turn on Kerberos debugging and output to this file

flags.name: krpc_port
flags.description: port on which KRPC based ImpalaInternalService is exported

flags.name: kudu_client_connection_negotiation_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Timeout for connection negotiation between Kudu client and Kudu masters and tablet servers, in milliseconds

flags.name: kudu_client_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Timeout (milliseconds) set for individual Kudu client rpcs. An operation may consist of several rpcs, so this is expected to be less than kudu_operation_timeout_ms. This must be a positive value or it will be ignored and Kudu's default of 10s will be used. There is no way to disable timeouts.

flags.name: kudu_operation_timeout_ms
flags.description: Timeout (milliseconds) set for all Kudu operations. This must be a positive value, and there is no way to disable timeouts.

flags.name: kudu_sasl_protocol_name
flags.description: SASL protocol name for Kudu

flags.name: load_auth_to_local_rules
flags.description: If true, load auth_to_local configuration from hdfs' core-site.xml. When enabled, impalad reads the rules from the property hadoop.security.auth_to_local and applies them to translate the Kerberos principal to its corresponding local user name for authorization.

flags.name: log_filename
flags.description: Prefix of log filename - full path is <log_dir>/<log_filename>.[INFO|WARN|ERROR|FATAL]

flags.name: log_rotation_match_pid
flags.description: If set to True, Impala log rotation will only consider log files that match with PID of currently running service. Otherwise, log rotation will ignore the PID in log file names and may remove older log files from previous PID run. Set to True if log files from prior run must be retained or when running multiple instances of same service with common log directory. Default to False.

flags.name: max_log_files
flags.description: Maximum number of log files to retain per severity level. The most recent log files are retained. If set to 0, all log files are retained.

flags.name: max_minidumps
flags.description: Maximum number of minidump files to keep per daemon. Older files are removed first. Set to 0 to keep all minidump files.

flags.name: mem_limit
flags.description: Limit on process memory consumption. Includes the JVM's memory consumption only if --mem_limit_includes_jvm is true. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the physical memory ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given.

flags.name: mem_limit_includes_jvm
flags.description: If true, --mem_limit will include the JVM's max heap size and committed memory in the process memory limit.

flags.name: min_buffer_size
flags.description: (Advanced) The minimum buffer size to use in the buffer pool

flags.name: min_privilege_set_for_show_stmts
flags.description: Comma separated list of privileges. Any one of them is required to show a database or table. Defaults to "any" which means if the user has any privilege (CREATE, SELECT, INSERT, etc) on a database or table, the database/table is visible in the results of SHOW DATABASES/TABLES. If set to "select", only dbs/tables on which the user has SELECT privilege will be shown. If set to "select,insert", only dbs/tables on which the user has SELECT or INSERT privilege will be shown. In practice, this flag can be set to "select" or "select,insert" to improve performance of SHOW DATABASES/TABLES and GET_SCHEMAS/GET_TABLES, especially when using Sentry and having thousands of candidate dbs/tables to be checked with a user with large scale of privileges. No significant performance gain when using Ranger

flags.name: minidump_path
flags.description: Directory to write minidump files to. This can be either an absolute path or a path relative to log_dir. Each daemon will create an additional sub-directory to prevent naming conflicts and to make it easier to identify a crashing daemon. Minidump files contain crash-related information in a compressed format and will be written when a daemon exits unexpectedly, for example on an unhandled exception or signal. It is also possible to create minidumps on demand without exiting the process by sending SIGUSR1. Set to empty to disable writing minidump files.

flags.name: minidump_size_limit_hint_kb
flags.description: Size limit hint for minidump files in KB. If a minidump exceeds this value, then breakpad will reduce the stack memory it collects for each thread from 8KB to 2KB. However it will always include the full stack memory for the first 20 threads, including the thread that crashed.

flags.name: mt_dop_auto_fallback
flags.description: Removed

flags.name: num_check_authorization_threads
flags.description: The number of threads used to check authorization for the user when executing show tables/databases. This configuration is applicable only when authorization is enabled. A value of 1 disables multi-threaded execution for checking authorization.However, a small value of larger than 1 may limit the parallelism of FE requests when checking authorization with a high concurrency. The value must be in the range of 1 to 128.

flags.name: principal
flags.description: Kerberos principal. If set, both client and backend network connections will use Kerberos encryption and authentication and the daemon will acquire a Kerberos TGT (i.e. do the equivalent of the kinit command) and keep it refreshed for the lifetime of the daemon.  If this is not set the TGT ticket will not be acquired and incoming connections will not be authenticated or encrypted using Kerberos. However, the TGT and other settings may be inherited from the environment and used by client libraries in certain cases.

flags.name: pull_table_types_and_comments
flags.description: When set, catalogd will always load the table types and comments at startup and in executing INVALIDATE METADATA commands. In other words, unloaded tables will not just contain the table names, but also the table types and comments. This is a catalogd-only flag. Required if users want GET_TABLES requests return correct table types or comments.

flags.name: re2_mem_limit
flags.description: Maximum bytes of memory to be used by re2's regex engine to hold the compiled form of the regexp. For more memory-consuming patterns, this can be set to be a higher number.Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of memory limit for RE2 max_mem opt ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given.Default to 8MB. Using percentage is discouraged.

flags.name: read_size
flags.description: (Advanced) The preferred I/O request size in bytes to issue to HDFS or the local filesystem. Increasing the read size will increase memory requirements. Decreasing the read size may decrease I/O throughput.

flags.name: redaction_rules_file
flags.description: Absolute path to sensitive data redaction rules. The rules will be applied to all log messages and query text shown in the Web UI and audit records. Query results will not be affected. Refer to the documentation for the rule file format.

flags.name: redirect_stdout_stderr
flags.description: If true, redirects stdout/stderr to INFO/ERROR log.

flags.name: reserved_words_version
flags.description: Reserved words compatibility version. Reserved words cannot be used as identifiers in SQL. This flag determines the impala version from which the reserved word list is taken. The value must be one of ["2.11.0", "3.0.0"].

flags.name: skip_external_kerberos_auth
flags.description: (Advanced) skip kerberos authentication for incoming external connections to this daemon, e.g. clients connecting to the HS2 interface. Only has an effect if --principal is set, i.e. Kerberos is enabled.

flags.name: skip_internal_kerberos_auth
flags.description: (Advanced) skip kerberos authentication for incoming internal connections from other daemons within the Impala cluster (i.e. impalads, statestored, catalogd). Must be set to the same value across all daemons. Only has an effect if --principal is set, i.e. Kerberos is enabled.

flags.name: spnego_keytab_file
flags.description: Absolute path to Kerberos keytab file for HTTP spnego. If it is empty, --keytab_file flag will be used.

flags.name: state_store_2_host
flags.description: hostname where second StatestoreService instance is running

flags.name: state_store_2_port
flags.description: port where second StatestoreService instance is running

flags.name: state_store_ha_port
flags.description: port where StatestoreHaService is running

flags.name: state_store_host
flags.description: hostname where StatestoreService is running

flags.name: state_store_port
flags.description: port where StatestoreService is running

flags.name: tcmalloc_max_total_thread_cache_bytes
flags.description: (Advanced) Bound on the total amount of bytes allocated to TCMalloc thread caches. If left at 0 (default), use the default value in TCMalloc library.

flags.name: tolerate_statestore_startup_delay
flags.description: If set to true, the subscriber is able to tolerate the delay of the statestore's availability. The subscriber's process will not exit if it cannot register with the specified statestore on startup. But instead it enters into Recovery mode, it will loop, sleep and retry till it successfully registers with the statestore.

flags.name: unlock_zorder_sort
flags.description: If true, enables using ZORDER option for SORT BY.

flags.name: update_catalogd_rpc_resend_interval_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Interval (in ms) with which the statestore resends the update catalogd RPC to a subscriber if the statestore has failed to send the RPC to the subscriber.

flags.name: use_resolved_hostname
flags.description: If true, --hostname is resolved before use, so that the IP address will be used everywhere instead of the hostname.

flags.name: use_subscriber_id_as_catalogd_priority
flags.description: Subscriber-id is used as priority value of catalogd instance if this is set as true. Otherwise, registration_id which is generated as random number will be used as priority value of catalogd instance.

flags.name: jvm_automatic_add_opens
flags.description: Adds necessary --add-opens options for core Java modules necessary to correctly calculate catalog metadata cache object sizes.

flags.name: local_library_dir
flags.description: Scratch space for local fs operations. Currently used for copying UDF binaries locally from HDFS and also for initializing the timezone db

flags.name: memory_maintenance_sleep_time_ms
flags.description: Sleep time in milliseconds between memory maintenance iterations

flags.name: pause_monitor_sleep_time_ms
flags.description: Sleep time in milliseconds for pause monitor thread.

flags.name: pause_monitor_warn_threshold_ms
flags.description: If the pause monitor sleeps more than this time period, a warning is logged. If set to 0 or less, pause monitor is disabled.

flags.name: data_source_batch_size
flags.description: Batch size for calls to GetNext() on external data sources.

flags.name: exchg_node_buffer_size_bytes
flags.description: (Advanced) Maximum size of per-query receive-side buffer

flags.name: enable_quadratic_probing
flags.description: Enable quadratic probing hash table

flags.name: always_use_data_cache
flags.description: (Advanced) Always uses the IO data cache for all reads, regardless of whether the read is local or remote. By default, the IO data cache is only used if the data is expected to be remote. Used by tests.

flags.name: max_row_batches
flags.description: the maximum number of batches to queue in multithreaded HDFS scans

flags.name: min_filter_reject_ratio
flags.description: (Advanced) If the percentage of rows rejected by a runtime filter drops below this value, the filter is disabled.

flags.name: enable_json_scanner
flags.description: If set false, disable reading from json format tables.

flags.name: kudu_max_row_batches
flags.description: The maximum size of the row batch queue,  for Kudu scanners.

flags.name: kudu_read_mode
flags.description: (Advanced) Sets the Kudu scan ReadMode. Supported Kudu read modes are READ_LATEST and READ_AT_SNAPSHOT. Can be overridden with the query option of the same name.

flags.name: kudu_scanner_keep_alive_period_sec
flags.description: The period at which Kudu Scanners should send keep-alive requests to the tablet server to ensure that scanners do not time out.

flags.name: kudu_error_buffer_size
flags.description: The size (bytes) of the Kudu client buffer for returning errors, with a min of 1KB.If the actual errors exceed this size the query will fail.

flags.name: kudu_ignore_conflicts
flags.description: Control whether Impala should ignore Kudu conflict error on duplicate and absent primary keys during write operations. If this flag is set to true and Kudu cluster supports ignore operations, Impala will use {INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE}_IGNORE operations of Kudu API. Otherwise, Impala will use regular {INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE} operations and logs any occurrences of such conflict error. See also kudu_ignore_conflicts_in_transaction flag.

flags.name: kudu_ignore_conflicts_in_transaction
flags.description: Control whether Kudu transaction should ignore conflict error on duplicate and absent primary keys during write operations. If set to true, the Kudu transaction will not be aborted for hitting such a conflict error. This flag is only considered if kudu_ignore_conflicts flag is true.

flags.name: kudu_mutation_buffer_size
flags.description: The size (bytes) of the Kudu client buffer for mutations.

flags.name: kudu_client_num_reactor_threads
flags.description: Number of threads the Kudu client can use to send rpcs to Kudu. Must be > 0.

flags.name: kudu_client_v
flags.description: If >= 0, used to set the verbose logging level on the Kudu client instead of using the value of -v

flags.name: max_page_header_size
flags.description: max parquet page header size in bytes

flags.name: max_queued_row_batch_bytes
flags.description: (Advanced) the maximum bytes of queued rows per multithreaded scan node.

flags.name: runtime_filter_wait_time_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) the maximum time, in ms, that a scan node will wait for expected runtime filters to arrive.

flags.name: enabled_hdfs_text_scanner_plugins
flags.description: (Advanced) whitelist of HDFS text scanner plugins that Impala will try to dynamically load. Must be a comma-separated list of upper-case compression codec names. Each plugin implements support for decompression and hands off the decompressed bytes to Impala's builtin text parser for further processing (e.g. parsing delimited text).

flags.name: partitioned_topn_in_mem_partitions_limit
flags.description: (Experimental) Soft limit on the number of in-memory partitions in an instance of the partitioned top-n operator.

flags.name: partitioned_topn_soft_limit_bytes
flags.description: (Experimental) Soft limit on the number of in-memory partitions in an instance of the partitioned top-n operator.

flags.name: ai_additional_platforms
flags.description: A comma-separated list of additional platforms allowed for Impala to access via the AI api, formatted as 'site1,site2'.

flags.name: ai_api_key_jceks_secret
flags.description: The jceks secret key used for extracting the api key from configured keystores. 'hadoop.security.credential.provider.path' in core-site must be configured to include the keystore storing the corresponding secret.

flags.name: ai_connection_timeout_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in seconds for connection timed out when communicating with an external AI engine

flags.name: ai_endpoint
flags.description: The default API endpoint for an external AI engine.

flags.name: ai_model
flags.description: The default AI model used by an external AI engine.

flags.name: hdfs_zone_alias_conf
flags.description: HDFS/S3A/ADLS path to config file defining non-standard time-zone aliases.

flags.name: hdfs_zone_info_zip
flags.description: HDFS/S3A/ADLS path to a zip archive of the IANA time-zone database to use.

flags.name: rpc_acceptor_listen_backlog
flags.description: Socket backlog parameter used when listening for RPC connections. This defines the maximum length to which the queue of pending TCP connections inbound to the RPC server may grow. If a connection request arrives when the queue is full, the client may receive an error. Higher values may help the server ride over bursts of new inbound connection requests.

flags.name: rpc_encrypt_loopback_connections
flags.description: Whether to encrypt data transfer on RPC connections that stay within a single host. Encryption here is likely to offer no additional security benefit since only a local 'root' user could intercept the traffic, and wire encryption does not suitably protect against such an attacker.

flags.name: rpc_negotiation_inject_delay_ms
flags.description: If enabled, injects the given number of milliseconds delay into the RPC negotiation process on the server side.

flags.name: rpc_trace_negotiation
flags.description: If enabled, dump traces of all RPC negotiations to the log

flags.name: rpc_callback_max_cycles
flags.description: The maximum number of cycles for which an RPC callback should be allowed to run without emitting a warning. (Advanced debugging option)

flags.name: rpc_inject_cancellation_state
flags.description: If this flag is not -1, it is the state in which a cancellation request will be injected. Should use values in OutboundCall::State only

flags.name: rpc_reopen_outbound_connections
flags.description: Open a new connection to the server for every RPC call. If not enabled, an already existing connection to a server is reused upon making another call to the same server. When this flag is enabled, an already existing _idle_ connection to the server is closed upon making another RPC call which would reuse the connection otherwise. Used by tests only.

flags.name: tcp_keepalive_probe_period_s
flags.description: The duration in seconds after an outbound connection has gone idle before a TCP keepalive probe is sent to the peer. Set to 0 to disable TCP keepalive probes from being sent.

flags.name: tcp_keepalive_retry_count
flags.description: The maximum number of keepalive probes sent before declaring the remote end as dead. Effective only if --tcp_keepalive_probe_period_s is not 0.

flags.name: tcp_keepalive_retry_period_s
flags.description: The duration in seconds between successive keepalive probes from an outbound connection if the previous probes are not acknowledged. Effective only if --tcp_keepalive_probe_period_s is not 0.

flags.name: remember_clients_ttl_ms
flags.description: Maximum amount of time, in milliseconds, the server "remembers" a client for the purpose of caching its responses. After this period without hearing from it, the client is no longer remembered and the memory occupied by its responses is reclaimed. Retries of requests older than 'remember_clients_ttl_ms' are treated as new ones.

flags.name: remember_responses_ttl_ms
flags.description: Maximum amount of time, in milliseconds, the server "remembers" a response to a specific request for a client. After this period has elapsed, the response may have been garbage collected and the client might get a response indicating the request is STALE.

flags.name: result_tracker_gc_interval_ms
flags.description: Interval at which the result tracker will look for entries to GC.

flags.name: rpc_dump_all_traces
flags.description: If true, dump all RPC traces at INFO level

flags.name: rpc_duration_too_long_ms
flags.description: Threshold (in milliseconds) above which a RPC is considered too long and its duration and method name are logged at INFO level. The time measured is between when a RPC is accepted and when its call handler completes.

flags.name: rpc_inject_invalid_authn_token_ratio
flags.description: If set higher than 0, AuthenticateByToken() randomly injects errors replying with FATAL_INVALID_AUTHENTICATION_TOKEN code. The flag's value corresponds to the probability of the fault injection event. Used for only for tests.

flags.name: rpc_inject_invalid_channel_bindings_ratio
flags.description: The ratio of injection of invalid channel bindings during connection negotiation. This is a test-only flag.

flags.name: rpc_send_channel_bindings
flags.description: Whether to send channel bindings in NegotiatePB response as prescribed by RFC 5929. This is a test-only flag.

flags.name: trusted_subnets
flags.description: A trusted subnet whitelist. If set explicitly, all unauthenticated or unencrypted connections are prohibited except the ones from the specified address blocks. Otherwise, private network (127.0.0.0/8, etc.) and local subnets of all local network interfaces will be used. Set it to '0.0.0.0/0' to allow unauthenticated/unencrypted connections from all remote IP addresses. However, if network access is not otherwise restricted by a firewall, malicious users may be able to gain unauthorized access.

flags.name: enable_exactly_once
flags.description: Whether to enable exactly once semantics.

flags.name: rpc_max_message_size_enable_validation
flags.description: Whether to turn off validation for --rpc_max_message_size flag. This is a test-only flag.

flags.name: use_system_auth_to_local
flags.description: When enabled, use the system krb5 library to map Kerberos principal names to local (short) usernames. If not enabled, the first component of the principal will be used as the short name. For example, 'kudu/foo.example.com@EXAMPLE' will map to 'kudu'.

flags.name: ipki_server_key_size
flags.description: the number of bits for server cert's private key. The server cert is used for TLS connections to and from clients and other servers.

flags.name: openssl_security_level_override
flags.description: if set to 0 or greater, overrides the security level for OpenSSL library of versions 1.1.0 and newer; for test purposes only

flags.name: disable_blockbloomfilter_avx2
flags.description: Disable AVX2 operations in BlockBloomFilter. This flag has no effect if the target CPU doesn't support AVX2 at run-time or BlockBloomFilter was built with a compiler that doesn't support AVX2.

flags.name: cache_force_single_shard
flags.description: Override all cache implementations to use just one shard

flags.name: cache_memtracker_approximation_ratio
flags.description: The MemTracker associated with a cache can accumulate error up to this ratio to improve performance. For tests.

flags.name: trace_to_console
flags.description: Trace pattern specifying which trace events should be dumped directly to the console

flags.name: crash_on_eio
flags.description: Kill the process if an I/O operation results in EIO. If false, I/O resulting in EIOs will return the status IOError and leave error-handling up to the caller.

flags.name: encrypt_data_at_rest
flags.description: Whether sensitive files should be encrypted on the file system.

flags.name: encryption_key_length
flags.description: Encryption key length.

flags.name: env_inject_eio
flags.description: Fraction of the time that operations on certain files will fail with the posix code EIO.

flags.name: env_inject_eio_globs
flags.description: Comma-separated list of glob patterns specifying files on which I/O will fail. By default, all files may cause a failure.

flags.name: env_inject_lock_failure_globs
flags.description: Comma-separated list of glob patterns specifying files on which attempts to obtain a file lock will fail. By default, no files will fail.

flags.name: env_inject_short_read_bytes
flags.description: The number of bytes less than the requested bytes to read

flags.name: env_inject_short_write_bytes
flags.description: The number of bytes less than the requested bytes to write

flags.name: env_use_fsync
flags.description: Use fsync(2) instead of fdatasync(2) for synchronizing dirty data to disk.

flags.name: env_use_ioctl_hole_punch_on_xfs
flags.description: Use the XFS_IOC_UNRESVSP64 ioctl instead of fallocate(2) to punch holes on XFS filesystems.

flags.name: never_fsync
flags.description: Never fsync() anything to disk. This is used by certain test cases to speed up runtime. This is very unsafe to use in production.

flags.name: disk_reserved_bytes_free_for_testing
flags.description: For testing only! Set to number of bytes free on each filesystem. Set to -1 to disable this test-specific override

flags.name: disk_reserved_override_prefix_1_bytes_free_for_testing
flags.description: For testing only! Set number of bytes free on the path prefix specified by --disk_reserved_override_prefix_1_path_for_testing. Set to -1 to disable.

flags.name: disk_reserved_override_prefix_1_path_for_testing
flags.description: For testing only! Specifies a prefix to override the visible 'bytes free' on. Use --disk_reserved_override_prefix_1_bytes_free_for_testing to set the number of bytes free for this path prefix. Set to empty string to disable.

flags.name: disk_reserved_override_prefix_2_bytes_free_for_testing
flags.description: For testing only! Set number of bytes free on the path prefix specified by --disk_reserved_override_prefix_2_path_for_testing. Set to -1 to disable.

flags.name: disk_reserved_override_prefix_2_path_for_testing
flags.description: For testing only! Specifies a prefix to override the visible 'bytes free' on. Use --disk_reserved_override_prefix_2_bytes_free_for_testing to set the number of bytes free for this path prefix. Set to empty string to disable.

flags.name: env_inject_full
flags.description: Fraction of the time that space checks on certain paths will yield the posix code ENOSPC.

flags.name: env_inject_full_globs
flags.description: Comma-separated list of glob patterns specifying which paths return with space errors.

flags.name: disable_core_dumps
flags.description: Disable core dumps when this process crashes.

flags.name: dump_metrics_json
flags.description: Dump a JSON document describing all of the metrics which may be emitted by this binary.

flags.name: dump_metrics_xml
flags.description: Dump an XML document describing all of the metrics which may be emitted by this binary.

flags.name: redact
flags.description: Comma-separated list that controls redaction context. Supported options are 'all','log', and 'none'. If 'all' is specified, sensitive data (sensitive configuration flags and row data) will be redacted from the web UI as well as glog and error messages. If 'log' is specified, sensitive data will only be redacted from glog and error messages. If 'none' is specified, no redaction will occur.

flags.name: umask
flags.description: The umask that will be used when creating files and directories. Permissions of top-level data directories will also be modified at start-up to conform to the given umask. Changing this value may enable unauthorized local users to read or modify data stored by Kudu.

flags.name: unlock_experimental_flags
flags.description: Unlock flags marked as 'experimental'. These flags are not guaranteed to be maintained across releases of Kudu, and may enable features or behavior known to be unstable. Use at your own risk.

flags.name: unlock_unsafe_flags
flags.description: Unlock flags marked as 'unsafe'. These flags are not guaranteed to be maintained across releases of Kudu, and enable features or behavior known to be unsafe. Use at your own risk.

flags.name: hung_task_check_interval_ms
flags.description: Number of milliseconds in between checks for hung threads

flags.name: inject_latency_on_kernel_stack_lookup_ms
flags.description: Number of milliseconds of latency to inject when reading a thread's kernel stack

flags.name: log_async
flags.description: Enable asynchronous writing to log files. This improves latency and stability.

flags.name: log_async_buffer_bytes_per_level
flags.description: The number of bytes of buffer space used by each log level. Only relevant when --log_async is enabled.

flags.name: allocator_aligned_mode
flags.description: Use 16-byte alignment instead of 8-byte, unless explicitly specified otherwise - to boost SIMD

flags.name: metrics_retirement_age_ms
flags.description: The minimum number of milliseconds a metric will be kept for after it is no longer active. (Advanced option)

flags.name: dns_resolver_cache_capacity_mb
flags.description: Capacity of DNS resolver cache, in MiBytes. For each key, the cache stores records returned by getaddrinfo(). A value of 0 means the results of DNS name resolution are not cached.

flags.name: dns_resolver_cache_ttl_sec
flags.description: TTL of records in the DNS resolver cache, in seconds.

flags.name: dns_resolver_max_threads_num
flags.description: The maximum number of threads to use for async DNS resolution

flags.name: dns_addr_resolution_override
flags.description: Comma-separated list of '='-separated pairs of hosts to addresses. The left-hand side of the '=' is taken as a host, and will resolve to the right-hand side which is expected to be a socket address with no port.

flags.name: fail_dns_resolution
flags.description: Whether to fail dns resolution, for tests.

flags.name: fail_dns_resolution_hostports
flags.description: Comma-separated list of hostports that fail dns resolution. If empty, fails all dns resolution attempts. Only takes effect if --fail_dns_resolution is 'true'.

flags.name: host_for_tests
flags.description: Host to use when resolving a given server's locally bound or advertised addresses.

flags.name: local_ip_for_outbound_sockets
flags.description: IP to bind to when making outgoing socket connections. This must be an IP address of the form A.B.C.D, not a hostname. Advanced parameter, subject to change.

flags.name: socket_inject_short_recvs
flags.description: Inject short recv() responses which return less data than requested

flags.name: memory_limit_hard_bytes
flags.description: Maximum amount of memory this daemon should use, in bytes. A value of 0 autosizes based on the total system memory. A value of -1 disables all memory limiting.

flags.name: memory_limit_soft_percentage
flags.description: Percentage of the hard memory limit that this daemon may consume before memory throttling of writes begins. The greater the excess, the higher the chance of throttling. In general, a lower soft limit leads to smoother write latencies but decreased throughput, and vice versa for a higher soft limit.

flags.name: memory_limit_warn_threshold_percentage
flags.description: Percentage of the hard memory limit that this daemon may consume before WARNING level messages are periodically logged.

flags.name: memory_pressure_percentage
flags.description: Percentage of the hard memory limit that this daemon may consume before flushing of in-memory data becomes prioritized.

flags.name: thread_inject_start_latency_ms
flags.description: Number of ms to sleep when starting a new thread. (For tests).

flags.name: accepted_cnxn_queue_depth
flags.description: (Advanced) The size of the post-accept, pre-setup connection queue in each thrift server set up to service Impala internal and external connections.

flags.name: accepted_cnxn_setup_thread_pool_size
flags.description: (Advanced) The size of the thread pool that is used to process the post-accept, pre-setup connection queue in each thrift server set up to service Impala internal and external connections.

flags.name: cookie_require_secure
flags.description: (Advanced) If true, authentication cookies will include the 'Secure' attribute, indicating to clients that they should only be returned over SSL connections. For testing only.

flags.name: max_cookie_lifetime_s
flags.description: Maximum amount of time in seconds that an authentication cookie will remain valid. Setting to 0 disables use of cookies. Defaults to 1 day.

flags.name: samesite_strict
flags.description: (Advanced) If true, authentication cookies will include SameSite=Strict.

flags.name: enable_group_filter_check_for_authenticated_kerberos_user
flags.description: If this configuration is set to true, Impala checks the provided LDAP group filter, if any, with the authenticated Kerberos user. This should be only enabled if both Kerberos and LDAP authentication are enabled and the users in KDC and LDAP are synchronized (e.g. when the KDC and the LDAP is the same Active Directory server). The default value is false, which provides backwards-compatible behavior.

flags.name: enable_ldap_auth
flags.description: If true, use LDAP authentication for client connections

flags.name: internal_principals_whitelist
flags.description: (Advanced) Comma-separated list of  additional usernames authorized to access Impala's internal APIs. Defaults to 'hdfs' which is the system user that in certain deployments must access catalog server APIs.

flags.name: jwks_ca_certificate
flags.description: File path of a pem bundle of root ca certificates that will be trusted when retrieving the JWKS from the specified JWKS URL.

flags.name: jwks_file_path
flags.description: File path of the pre-installed JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) for JWT verification

flags.name: jwks_pulling_timeout_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in seconds for connection timed out when pulling JWKS from the specified URL.

flags.name: jwks_update_frequency_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in seconds to wait between downloading JWKS from the specified URL.

flags.name: jwks_url
flags.description: URL of the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) for JWT verification

flags.name: jwks_verify_server_certificate
flags.description: Specifies if the TLS certificate of the JWKS server is verified when retrieving the JWKS from the specified JWKS URL.  A certificate is considered valid if a trust chain can be established for it, and if the certificate has a common name or SAN that matches the server's hostname. This should only be set to false for development / testing.

flags.name: jwt_custom_claim_username
flags.description: Custom claim 'username'

flags.name: jwt_token_auth
flags.description: When true, read the JWT token out of the HTTP Header and extract user name from the token payload.

flags.name: jwt_validate_signature
flags.description: When true, validate the signature of JWT token with pre-installed JWKS.

flags.name: ldap_ca_certificate
flags.description: The full path to the certificate file used to authenticate the LDAP server's certificate for SSL / TLS connections.

flags.name: ldap_group_filter
flags.description: Used as filter for both simple and search bind mechanisms. For simple bind it is a comma separated list of groups. If specified, users must belong to one of these groups for authentication to succeed. For search bind it is an LDAP filter that will be used during LDAP group search, it can contain '{0}' pattern which will be replaced with the user name and/or '{1}' which will be replace with the user dn.

flags.name: ldap_user_filter
flags.description: Used as filter for both simple and search bind mechanisms. For simple bind it is a comma separated list of user names. If specified, users must be on this list for authentication to succeed. For search bind it is an LDAP filter that will be used during LDAP search, it can contain '{0}' pattern which will be replaced with the user name.

flags.name: oauth_jwks_ca_certificate
flags.description: File path of a pem bundle of root ca certificates that will be trusted when retrieving the JWKS from the specified JWKS URL.

flags.name: oauth_jwks_file_path
flags.description: File path of the pre-installed JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) for OAuth verification

flags.name: oauth_jwks_pulling_timeout_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in seconds for connection timed out when verifying OAuth token from the specified OAuth server.

flags.name: oauth_jwks_update_frequency_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in seconds to wait for refreshing the OAuth token from the OAuth URL.

flags.name: oauth_jwks_url
flags.description: URL of the OAuth Endpoint for token verification

flags.name: oauth_jwks_verify_server_certificate
flags.description: Specifies if the TLS certificate of the JWKS server is verified when retrieving the JWKS from the specified JWKS URL.  A certificate is considered valid if a trust chain can be established for it, and if the certificate has a common name or SAN that matches the server's hostname. This should only be set to false for development / testing.

flags.name: oauth_jwt_custom_claim_username
flags.description: Custom claim of the token that contains the username

flags.name: oauth_jwt_validate_signature
flags.description: When true, validate the signature of OAuth token with pre-installed JWKS.This should only be set to false for development / testing

flags.name: oauth_token_auth
flags.description: When true, read the OAuth token out of the HTTP Header and extract user name from the token payload.

flags.name: sasl_path
flags.description: Colon separated list of paths to look for SASL security library plugins.

flags.name: trusted_auth_header
flags.description: If set as non empty string, Impala will look for this header in the HTTP headers. If the header is present, Impala will skip authentication and extract the username directly from the authorization header. Currently, only connections over HTTP support this. Note: It still requires the client to specify a username via the Basic Authorization header in the format <username>:<password> where the password is not used and can be left blank. Warning: Only use this flag if the connections are authenticated before the requests land on Impala so that Impala can avoid the authentication again. The system must remove the trusted HTTP headers from any requests that come from outside the system.

flags.name: trusted_domain
flags.description: If set, Impala will skip authentication for connections originating from this domain. Currently, only connections over HTTP support this. Note: It still requires the client to specify a username via the Basic Authorization header in the format <username>:<password> where the password is not used and can be left blank.

flags.name: trusted_domain_empty_xff_header_use_origin
flags.description: If set to true and the 'X-Forwarded-For' HTTP header value is empty in the request, then the origin of the the underlying transport is used while attempting to verify if the connection request originated from a trusted domain. Only used if '--trusted_domain' and '--trusted_domain_use_xff_header' flags are specified. Warning: In case the 'X-Forwarded-For' HTTP header is empty or not in the request, this flag allows a fallback to the default behavior in trusted domain check (where '--trusted_domain' flag is specified, but '--trusted_domain_use_xff_header' flag is not set).

flags.name: trusted_domain_strict_localhost
flags.description: If set to true and trusted_domain='localhost', this will not use reverse DNS to determine if something is from localhost. It will only match 127.0.0.1. This is important for security, because reverse DNS can resolve other non-local addresses to localhost.

flags.name: trusted_domain_use_xff_header
flags.description: If set to true, this uses the 'X-Forwarded-For' HTTP header to check for origin while attempting to verify if the connection request originated from a trusted domain. Only used if '--trusted_domain' is specified. Warning: Only use this if you trust the incoming connection to have this set correctly.

flags.name: use_xff_address_as_origin
flags.description: If set to true use the address in 'X-Forwarded-For' HTTP header as origin of the connection. If XFF header is not set then the Peer Address on the underlying socket is used as the origin. If XFF header has multiple addresses corresponding to the various intermediate proxies, then the first address is used as the origin. XFF header with multiple IP addresses must be comma separated. Only use this if you trust the incoming connection to have the XFF header set correctly.

flags.name: num_acceptor_threads
flags.description: Number of threads dedicated to accepting connection requests for RPC services

flags.name: num_reactor_threads
flags.description: Number of threads dedicated to managing network IO for RPC services. If left at default value 0, it will be set to number of CPU cores.

flags.name: rpc_negotiation_thread_count
flags.description: Maximum number of threads dedicated to handling RPC connection negotiations.

flags.name: rpc_negotiation_timeout_ms
flags.description: Time in milliseconds of waiting for a negotiation to complete before timing out.

flags.name: rpc_retry_interval_ms
flags.description: Time in millisecond of waiting before retrying an RPC when remote is busy

flags.name: rpc_use_loopback
flags.description: Always use loopback for local connections. This requires binding to all addresses, not just the KRPC address.

flags.name: rpc_use_unix_domain_socket
flags.description: Whether the KRPC client and server should use Unix domain socket. If enabled, each daemon is identified with Unix Domain Socket address in the unique name in "Abstract Namespace", in format @impala-krpc:<BackendId>. The KRPC server bind to a Unix domain socket. KRPC Client attempt to connect to KRPC server via a Unix domain socket.

flags.name: uds_address_unique_id
flags.description: Specify unique Id for UDS address. It could be "ip_address", "backend_id", or "none"

flags.name: thrift_external_rpc_max_message_size
flags.description: The maximum size of a message for external client RPC communication. This defaults to 2GB to limit the impact of untrusted payloads. This must be set to at least the default defined in Thrift (100MB). Setting 0 or a negative value will use the default defined in Thrift.

flags.name: thrift_rpc_max_message_size
flags.description: The maximum size of a message for intra-cluster RPC communication between Impala components. Default to a high limit of 64GB. This must be set to at least the default defined in Thrift (100MB). Setting 0 or a negative value will use the default defined in Thrift.

flags.name: concurrent_scratch_ios_per_device
flags.description: Set this to influence the number of concurrent write I/Os issues to write data to scratch files. This is multiplied by the number of active scratch directories to obtain the target number of scratch write I/Os per query.

flags.name: madvise_huge_pages
flags.description: (Advanced) If true, advise operating system to back large memory buffers with huge pages

flags.name: mmap_buffers
flags.description: (Experimental) If true, allocate buffers directly from the operating system instead of with TCMalloc.

flags.name: insert_inherit_permissions
flags.description: If true, new directories created by INSERTs will inherit the permissions of their parent directories

flags.name: admission_control_slots
flags.description: (Advanced) The maximum degree of parallelism to run queries with on this backend. This determines the number of slots available to queries in admission control for this backend. The degree of parallelism of the query determines the number of slots that it needs. Defaults to number of cores / -num_cores for executors, and 8x that value for dedicated coordinators).

flags.name: backend_client_connection_num_retries
flags.description: Retry backend connections.

flags.name: backend_client_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for a backend client RPC.

flags.name: catalog_client_connection_num_retries
flags.description: The number of times connections or RPCs to the catalog should be retried.

flags.name: catalog_client_rpc_retry_interval_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The time to wait before retrying when the catalog RPC client fails to connect to catalogd or when RPCs to the catalogd fail.

flags.name: catalog_client_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for a catalog client RPC. The default is 10 hours. Operations take longer than this are usually abnormal and hanging.

flags.name: catalog_lightweight_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for a lightweight catalog RPC which shouldn't take long in catalogd, e.g. fetching db/table list. The default is 30 minutes which is long enough to tolerate TCP timeout due to retransmission.

flags.name: catalog_service_host
flags.description: hostname where CatalogService is running

flags.name: codegen_cache_capacity
flags.description: Specify the capacity of the codegen cache. If set to 0, codegen cache is disabled.

flags.name: enable_webserver
flags.description: If true, debug webserver is enabled

flags.name: local_catalog_cache_concurrency_level
flags.description: If --use_local_catalog is enabled, configures the local cache's concurrency level to avoid lock contention, the default value 4 is consistent with the default value of the original cache.

flags.name: local_catalog_cache_expiration_s
flags.description: If --use_local_catalog is enabled, configures the expiration time of the catalog cache within each impalad. Even if the configured cache capacity has not been reached, items are removed from the cache if they have not been accessed in this amount of time.

flags.name: local_catalog_cache_mb
flags.description: If --use_local_catalog is enabled, configures the size of the catalog cache within each impalad. If this is set to -1, the cache is auto-configured to 60% of the configured Java heap size. Note that the Java heap size is distinct from and typically smaller than the overall Impala memory limit.

flags.name: local_catalog_max_fetch_retries
flags.description: If --use_local_catalog is enabled, configures the maximum number of times the frontend retries when fetching a metadata object from the impalad coordinator's local catalog cache.

flags.name: max_concurrent_queries
flags.description: (Deprecated) This has been replaced with --admission_control_slots, which better accounts for the higher parallelism of queries with mt_dop > 1. If --admission_control_slots is not set, the value of --max_concurrent_queries is used instead for backward compatibility.

flags.name: metrics_webserver_interface
flags.description: Interface to start metrics webserver on. If blank, webserver binds to 0.0.0.0

flags.name: metrics_webserver_port
flags.description: If non-zero, the port to run the metrics webserver on, which exposes the /metrics, /jsonmetrics, /metrics_prometheus, and /healthz endpoints without authentication enabled.

flags.name: num_hdfs_worker_threads
flags.description: (Advanced) The number of threads in the global HDFS operation pool

flags.name: ping_expose_webserver_url
flags.description: If true, debug webserver url is exposed via PingImpalaService/PingImpalaHS2Service RPC calls

flags.name: state_store_subscriber_port
flags.description: port where StatestoreSubscriberService should be exported

flags.name: use_local_catalog
flags.description: Use the on-demand metadata feature in coordinators. If this is set, coordinators pull metadata as needed from catalogd and cache it locally. The cached metadata gets evicted automatically under memory pressure or after an expiration time.

flags.name: s3a_access_key_cmd
flags.description: A Unix command whose output returns the access key to S3, i.e. "fs.s3a.access.key".

flags.name: s3a_secret_key_cmd
flags.description: A Unix command whose output returns the secret key to S3, i.e. "fs.s3a.secret.key".

flags.name: data_cache_anonymize_trace
flags.description: (Advanced) Use hashes of filenames rather than file paths in the data cache access trace.

flags.name: data_cache_async_write_buffer_limit
flags.description: (Experimental) Limit of the total buffer size used by asynchronous store tasks.

flags.name: data_cache_checksum
flags.description: (Advanced) Enable checksumming for the cached buffer.

flags.name: data_cache_enable_tracing
flags.description: (Advanced) Collect a trace of all lookups in the data cache.

flags.name: data_cache_eviction_policy
flags.description: (Advanced) The cache eviction policy to use for the data cache. Either 'LRU' (default) or 'LIRS' (experimental)

flags.name: data_cache_file_max_size_bytes
flags.description: (Advanced) The maximum size which a cache file can grow to before data stops being appended to it.

flags.name: data_cache_max_opened_files
flags.description: (Advanced) The maximum number of allowed opened files. This must be at least the number of specified partitions.

flags.name: data_cache_trace_dir
flags.description: The base directory for data cache tracing. The data cache trace files for each cache directory are placed in separate subdirectories underneath this base directory. If blank, defaults to <log_file_dir>/data_cache_trace/

flags.name: data_cache_trace_percentage
flags.description: The percentage of cache lookups that should be emitted to the trace file.

flags.name: data_cache_write_concurrency
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of concurrent threads allowed to insert into the cache per partition; unset uses 1 for rotational disks and 8 for solid state disks.

flags.name: max_data_cache_trace_file_size
flags.description: The maximum size (in log entries) of the data cache trace file before a new one is created.

flags.name: max_data_cache_trace_files
flags.description: Maximum number of data cache trace files to retain for each cache directory specified by the data_cache startup parameter. The most recent trace files are retained. If set to 0, all trace files are retained.

flags.name: cache_abfs_file_handles
flags.description: Enable the file handle cache for ABFS files.

flags.name: cache_ozone_file_handles
flags.description: Enable the file handle cache for Ozone files.

flags.name: cache_remote_file_handles
flags.description: Enable the file handle cache for remote HDFS files.

flags.name: cache_s3_file_handles
flags.description: Enable the file handle cache for S3 files.

flags.name: data_cache
flags.description: The configuration string for IO data cache. Default to be an empty string so it's disabled. The configuration string is expected to be a list of directories, separated by ',', followed by a ':' and a capacity quota per directory. For example /data/0,/data/1:1TB means the cache may use up to 2TB, with 1TB max in /data/0 and /data/1 respectively. Please note that each Impala daemon on a host must have a unique caching directory.

flags.name: data_cache_keep_across_restarts
flags.description: (Experimental) If this is true, the data cache metadata is dumped to the same directory as the cached files on disk when the process gracefully shutdowns. The metadata will be reloaded the next time the process starts, so that the previous cached data can be reused as if the process had never shutdown. If loading fails, it will proceed with regular initialization.

flags.name: data_cache_num_async_write_threads
flags.description: (Experimental) Number of data cache async write threads. Write threads will write the cache asynchronously after IO thread read data, so IO thread will return more quickly. The extra memory for temporary buffers is limited by --data_cache_async_write_buffer_limit. If this's 0, then write will be synchronous.

flags.name: max_cached_file_handles
flags.description: Maximum number of HDFS file handles that will be cached. Disabled if set to 0.

flags.name: num_abfs_io_threads
flags.description: Number of ABFS I/O threads

flags.name: num_adls_io_threads
flags.description: Number of ADLS I/O threads

flags.name: num_cos_io_threads
flags.description: Number of COS I/O threads

flags.name: num_disks
flags.description: Number of disks on data node.

flags.name: num_file_handle_cache_partitions
flags.description: Number of partitions used by the file handle cache.

flags.name: num_gcs_io_threads
flags.description: Number of GCS I/O threads

flags.name: num_io_threads_per_rotational_disk
flags.description: Number of I/O threads per rotational disk. Has priority over num_threads_per_disk. If neither is set, defaults to 1 thread(s) per rotational disk

flags.name: num_io_threads_per_solid_state_disk
flags.description: Number of I/O threads per solid state disk. Has priority over num_threads_per_disk. If neither is set, defaults to 8 thread(s) per solid state disk

flags.name: num_obs_io_threads
flags.description: Number of OBS I/O threads

flags.name: num_oss_io_threads
flags.description: Number of OSS/JindoFS I/O threads

flags.name: num_ozone_io_threads
flags.description: Number of Ozone I/O threads

flags.name: num_remote_hdfs_file_oper_io_threads
flags.description: Number of remote HDFS file operations I/O threads

flags.name: num_remote_hdfs_io_threads
flags.description: Number of remote HDFS I/O threads

flags.name: num_s3_file_oper_io_threads
flags.description: Number of S3 file operations I/O threads

flags.name: num_s3_io_threads
flags.description: Number of S3 I/O threads

flags.name: num_sfs_io_threads
flags.description: Number of SFS I/O threads

flags.name: num_threads_per_disk
flags.description: Number of I/O threads per disk

flags.name: unused_file_handle_timeout_sec
flags.description: Maximum time, in seconds, that an unused HDFS file handle will remain in the file handle cache. Disabled if set to 0.

flags.name: fs_slow_read_log_threshold_ms
flags.description: Log diagnostics about I/Os issued via the HDFS client that take longer than this threshold.

flags.name: fs_trace_remote_reads
flags.description: (Advanced) Log block locations for remote reads.

flags.name: use_hdfs_pread
flags.description: Enables using hdfsPread() instead of hdfsRead() when performing HDFS read operations. This is necessary to use HDFS hedged reads (assuming the HDFS client is configured to do so). Preads are always enabled for S3A and ABFS reads.

flags.name: hdfs_operation_timeout_sec
flags.description: Maximum time, in seconds, that an HDFS operation should wait before timing out and failing.

flags.name: datastream_sender_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The time, in ms, that can elapse  before a plan fragment will time-out trying to send the initial row batch.

flags.name: datastream_service_deserialization_queue_size
flags.description: Number of deferred RPC requests that can be enqueued before being processed by a deserialization thread.

flags.name: datastream_service_num_deserialization_threads
flags.description: Number of threads for deserializing RPC requests deferred due to the receiver not ready or the soft limit of the receiver is reached.

flags.name: data_stream_sender_buffer_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Max size in bytes which a row batch in a data stream sender's channel can accumulate before the row batch is sent over the wire.

flags.name: dump_exec_request_path
flags.description: If set, dump TExecRequest structures to {dump_exec_request_path}/TExecRequest-{internal|external}.{query_id.hi}-{query_id.lo}

flags.name: log_mem_usage_interval
flags.description: If non-zero, impalad will output memory usage every log_mem_usage_interval'th fragment completion.

flags.name: query_exec_mgr_cancellation_thread_pool_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Size of the QueryExecMgr thread-pool processing cancellations due to coordinator failure

flags.name: max_filter_error_rate
flags.description: (Advanced) The target false positive probability used to determine the ideal size for each bloom filter size. This value can be overriden by the RUNTIME_FILTER_ERROR_RATE query option.

flags.name: max_error_logs_per_instance
flags.description: Maximum number of non-fatal error to be logged in log level 1 (INFO). Once this number exceeded, further non-fatal error will be logged at log level 2 (DEBUG) severity. This flag is ignored if user set negative max_errors query option. Default to 2000

flags.name: num_threads_per_core
flags.description: Number of threads per core.

flags.name: allow_multiple_scratch_dirs_per_device
flags.description: If false and --scratch_dirs contains multiple directories on the same device, then only the first writable directory is used

flags.name: disk_spill_compression_buffer_limit_bytes
flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on the total bytes of compression buffers that will be used for spill-to-disk compression across all queries. If this limit is exceeded, some data may be spilled to disk in uncompressed form.

flags.name: disk_spill_compression_codec
flags.description: (Advanced) If set, data will be compressed using the specified compression codec before spilling to disk. This can substantially reduce scratch disk usage, at the cost of requiring more CPU and memory resources to compress the data. Uses the same syntax as the COMPRESSION_CODEC query option, e.g. 'lz4', 'zstd', 'zstd:6'. If this is set, then --disk_spill_punch_holes must be enabled.

flags.name: disk_spill_encryption
flags.description: Set this to encrypt and perform an integrity check on all data spilled to disk during a query

flags.name: disk_spill_punch_holes
flags.description: (Advanced) changes the free space management strategy for files created in --scratch_dirs to punch holes in the file when space is unused. This can reduce the amount of scratch space used by queries, particularly in conjunction with disk spill compression. This option requires the filesystems of the directories in --scratch_dirs to support hole punching.

flags.name: remote_batch_read
flags.description: Set if the system uses batch reading for the remote temporary files. Batch readingallows reading a block asynchronously when the buffer pool is trying to pin onepage of that block.

flags.name: remote_read_memory_buffer_size
flags.description: Specify the maximum size of read memory buffers for the remote temporary files. Only valid when --remote_batch_read is true.

flags.name: remote_tmp_file_block_size
flags.description: Specify the size of the block for doing file uploading and fetching. The block size should be power of 2 and less than the size of remote temporary file.

flags.name: remote_tmp_file_size
flags.description: Specify the size of a remote temporary file. Upper bound is 256MB. Lower bound is the block size. The size should be power of 2 and integer times of the block size.

flags.name: remote_tmp_files_avail_pool_lifo
flags.description: If true, lifo is the algo to evict the local buffer files during spilling to the remote. Otherwise, fifo would be used.

flags.name: scratch_dirs
flags.description: Writable scratch directories. This is a comma-separated list of directories. Each directory is specified as the directory path, an optional limit on the bytes that will be allocated in that directory, and an optional priority for the directory. If the optional limit is provided, the path and the limit are separated by a colon. E.g. '/dir1:10G,/dir2:5GB,/dir3' will allow allocating up to 10GB of scratch in /dir1, 5GB of scratch in /dir2 and an unlimited amount in /dir3. If the optional priority is provided, the path and the limit and priority are separated by colon. Priority based spilling will result in directories getting selected as a spill target based on their priority. The lower the numerical value the higher the priority. E.g. '/dir1:10G:0,/dir2:5GB:1,/dir3::1', will cause spilling to first fill up '/dir1' followed by using '/dir2' and '/dir3' in a round robin manner.

flags.name: wait_for_spill_buffer_timeout_s
flags.description: Specify the timeout duration waiting for the buffer to write (second). If a spillingopertion fails to get a buffer from the pool within the duration, the operationfails.

flags.name: allow_tuple_caching
flags.description: If false, tuple caching cannot be used.

flags.name: tuple_cache
flags.description: The configuration string for the tuple cache. The default is the empty string, which disables the tuple cache. The configuration string is expected to be a directory followed by a ':' and a capacity quota. For example, /data/0:1TB means the cache may use 1TB in /data/0. Please note that each Impala daemon on a host must have a unique cache directory.

flags.name: tuple_cache_debug_dump_dir
flags.description: Directory for dumping the intermediate query result tuples for debugging purpose.

flags.name: tuple_cache_eviction_policy
flags.description: (Advanced) The cache eviction policy to use for the tuple cache. Either 'LRU' (default) or 'LIRS' (experimental)

flags.name: admission_control_service_num_svc_threads
flags.description: Number of threads for processing admission control service's RPCs. if left at default value 0, it will be set to number of CPU cores. Set it to a positive value to change from the default.

flags.name: admission_control_service_queue_mem_limit
