flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on RPC payloads consumption for AdmissionControlService. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the process memory limit ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given.

flags.name: admission_service_host
flags.description: If provided, queries submitted to this impalad will be scheduled and admitted by contacting the admission control service at the specified address and --admission_service_port.

flags.name: admission_status_wait_time_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The number of milliseconds the GetQueryStatus() rpc in the admission control service will wait for admission to complete before returning.

flags.name: admission_thread_pool_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Size of the thread-pool processing AdmitQuery requests.

flags.name: max_admission_queue_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Max size of the queue for the AdmitQuery thread pool.

flags.name: balance_queries_across_executor_groups
flags.description: If true, balance queries across multiple groups that belonging to the same request pool based on available memory and slots in each executor group. If false, admission is attempted to groups in alphanumerically sorted order.

flags.name: clamp_query_mem_limit_backend_mem_limit
flags.description: Caps query memory limit to memory limit for admission on the backends. The coordinator memory limit is capped to the coordinator backend's memory limit, while executor memory limit is capped to the effective or minimum memory limit for admission on executor backends. If the flag is not set, a query requesting more than backend's memory limit for admission gets rejected during admission. However, if this flag is set, such a query gets admitted with backend's memory limit and could succeed if the memory request was over estimated and could fail if query really needs more memory.

flags.name: cluster_membership_topic_id
flags.description: Specifies an identifier string that will be used as a prefix to Statestore topic ids used for grouping Impala backends and Admission Daemons into sub-groups within an Impala cluster defined by the Statestore service.

flags.name: queue_wait_timeout_ms
flags.description: Maximum amount of time (in milliseconds) that a request will wait to be admitted before timing out.

flags.name: admission_service_port
flags.description: The port where the admission control service runs

flags.name: blacklisting_enabled
flags.description: (Advanced) If false, disables local blacklisting of executors by coordinators, which temporarily removes executors that appear to be problematic from scheduling decisions.

flags.name: admission_max_retry_time_s
flags.description: (Advanced) The amount of time in seconds the coordinator will spend attempting to retry admission if the admissiond is unreachable.

flags.name: admission_status_retry_time_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The number of milliseconds coordinators will wait before retrying the GetQueryStatus rpc.

flags.name: default_pool_max_queued
flags.description: Maximum number of requests allowed to be queued before rejecting requests. A negative value or 0 indicates requests will always be rejected once the maximum number of concurrent requests are executing. Ignored if fair_scheduler_config_path and llama_site_path are set.

flags.name: default_pool_max_requests
flags.description: Maximum number of concurrent outstanding requests allowed to run before queueing incoming requests. A negative value indicates no limit. 0 indicates no requests will be admitted. Ignored if fair_scheduler_config_path and llama_site_path are set.

flags.name: default_pool_mem_limit
flags.description: Maximum amount of memory that all outstanding requests in this pool may use before new requests to this pool are queued. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the physical memory ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given. Ignored if fair_scheduler_config_path and llama_site_path are set.

flags.name: disable_pool_max_requests
flags.description: Disables all per-pool limits on the maximum number of running requests.

flags.name: disable_pool_mem_limits
flags.description: Disables all per-pool mem limits.

flags.name: fair_scheduler_allocation_path
flags.description: Path to the fair scheduler allocation file (fair-scheduler.xml).

flags.name: llama_site_path
flags.description: Path to the Llama configuration file (llama-site.xml). If set, fair_scheduler_allocation_path must also be set.

flags.name: require_username
flags.description: Requires that a user be provided in order to schedule requests. If enabled and a user is not provided, requests will be rejected, otherwise requests without a username will be submitted with the username 'default'.

flags.name: control_service_num_svc_threads
flags.description: Number of threads for processing control service's RPCs. if left at default value 0, it will be set to number of CPU cores. Set it to a positive value to change from the default.

flags.name: control_service_queue_mem_limit
flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on RPC payloads consumption for ControlService. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the process memory limit ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given.

flags.name: control_service_queue_mem_limit_floor_bytes
flags.description: Lower bound on --control_service_queue_mem_limit in bytes. If --control_service_queue_mem_limit works out to be less than this amount, this value is used instead

flags.name: datastream_service_num_svc_threads
flags.description: Number of threads for processing datastream services' RPCs. If left at default value 0, it will be set to number of CPU cores.  Set it to a positive value to change from the default.

flags.name: datastream_service_queue_mem_limit
flags.description: (Advanced) Limit on RPC payloads consumption for DataStreamService. Specified as number of bytes ('<int>[bB]?'), megabytes ('<float>[mM]'), gigabytes ('<float>[gG]'), or percentage of the process memory limit ('<int>%'). Defaults to bytes if no unit is given.

flags.name: allow_catalog_cache_op_from_masked_users
flags.description: Whether to allow table level catalog-cache operations, i.e. REFRESH/INVALIDATE METADATA <table>, from users that have associate Ranger masking policies on the table. By default, such operations are blocked since such users are considered read-only users. Note that checking column masking policies requires loading column info of the table, which could slow down simple commands like INVALIDATE METADATA <table>

flags.name: authorization_factory_class
flags.description: Specifies the class name that implements the authorization provider. This will override the authorization_provider flag if both are specified.

flags.name: authorization_provider
flags.description: Specifies the type of internally-provided authorization provider to use. Defaults to unset, which disables authorization. To enable authorization, set to one of the following: ['ranger']

flags.name: authorized_proxy_group_config
flags.description: Specifies the set of authorized proxy groups (users who can delegate to other users belonging to the specified groups during authorization) and whom they are allowed to delegate. Input is a semicolon-separated list of key=value pairs of authorized proxy users to the group(s) they can delegate to. These groups are specified as a list of groups separated by a delimiter (which defaults to comma and may be changed via --authorized_proxy_group_config_delimiter), or '*' to indicate all users. For example: hue=group1,group2;admin=*

flags.name: authorized_proxy_group_config_delimiter
flags.description: Specifies the delimiter used in authorized_proxy_group_config.

flags.name: authorized_proxy_user_config
flags.description: Specifies the set of authorized proxy users (users who can delegate to other users during authorization) and whom they are allowed to delegate. Input is a semicolon-separated list of key=value pairs of authorized proxy users to the user(s) they can delegate to. These users are specified as a list of short usernames separated by a delimiter (which defaults to comma and may be changed via --authorized_proxy_user_config_delimiter), or '*' to indicate all users. For example: hue=user1,user2;admin=*

flags.name: authorized_proxy_user_config_delimiter
flags.description: Specifies the delimiter used in authorized_proxy_user_config.

flags.name: dbcp_data_source_idle_timeout_s
flags.description: Timeout value in seconds for idle DBCP DataSource objects in cache. It only takes effect when query option 'clean_dbcp_ds_cache' is set as false.

flags.name: dbcp_max_conn_pool_size
flags.description: The maximum number of active connections that can be allocated from a DBCP connection pool at the same time, or -1 for no limit. DBCP connection pools are created when accessing remote RDBMS for external JDBC tables. This setting applies to all DBCP connection pools created on the coordinator.

flags.name: dbcp_max_wait_millis_for_conn
flags.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that DBCP connection pool will wait (when there are no available connections) for a connection to be returned before throwing an exception, or -1 to wait indefinitely. 0 means immediately throwing exception if there are no available connections in the pool.

flags.name: enable_kudu_impala_hms_check
flags.description: By default this flag is true. If enabled checks that Kudu and Impala are using the same HMS instance(s).

flags.name: enable_shell_based_groups_mapping_support
flags.description: Enables support for Hadoop groups mapping org.apache.hadoop.security.ShellBasedUnixGroupsMapping. By default this support is not enabled as it can lead to many process getting spawned to fetch groups for user using shell command.

flags.name: jni_frontend_class
flags.description: By default the JniFrontend class included in the repository is used as the frontend interface. This option allows the class to be overridden by a third party module. The overridden class needs to contain all the methods in the methods[] variable, so most implementations should make their class a child of JniFrontend and override only relevant methods.

flags.name: kudu_master_hosts
flags.description: Specifies the default Kudu master(s). The given value should be a comma separated list of hostnames or IP addresses; ports are optional.

flags.name: ranger_app_id
flags.description: Specifies the Ranger application ID. Ranger application ID is an ID to uniquely identify the application that communicates with Ranger. This flag is required when authorization with Ranger is enabled.

flags.name: ranger_service_type
flags.description: Specifies the Ranger service type.

flags.name: server_name
flags.description: The name to use for securing this impalad server during authorization. Set to enable authorization.

flags.name: trusted_jar_paths
flags.description: Comma-separated list of URI/path prefixes that are considered safe locations from which Impala may download and load jar files. When a 'driver.url' table property for JDBC data source tables, or the LOCATION for external data source tables, starts with one of these prefixes the jar is downloaded and loaded. An empty value (the default) disables jar loading entirely. Example: 'hdfs://namenode/trusted/jars/,s3://my-bucket/allowed-jars/'

flags.name: abort_on_failed_audit_event
flags.description: Shutdown Impala if there is a problem recording an audit event.

flags.name: abort_on_failed_lineage_event
flags.description: Shutdown Impala if there is a problem recording a lineage record.

flags.name: accepted_client_cnxn_timeout
flags.description: (Advanced) The amount of time in milliseconds an accepted connection will wait in the post-accept, pre-setup connection queue before it is timed out and the connection request is rejected. A value of 0 means there is no timeout.

flags.name: admission_heartbeat_frequency_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The time in milliseconds to wait between sending heartbeats to the admission service, if enabled. Heartbeats are used to ensure resources are properly accounted for even if rpcs to the admission service occasionally fail.

flags.name: audit_event_log_dir
flags.description: The directory in which audit event log files are written. Setting this flag will enable audit event logging.

flags.name: auto_check_compaction
flags.description: When true, compaction checking will be conducted for each query in local catalog mode. Note that this checking introduces additional overhead because Impala makes additional RPCs to hive metastore for each table in a query during the query compilation.

flags.name: beeswax_port
flags.description: port on which Beeswax client requests are served.If 0 or less, the Beeswax server is not started. This interface is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

flags.name: cancellation_thread_pool_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Size of the thread-pool processing cancellations due to node failure

flags.name: client_keepalive_probe_period_s
flags.description: The duration in seconds after a client connection has gone idle before a TCP keepalive probe is sent to the client. Set to 0 to disable TCP keepalive probes from being sent.

flags.name: client_keepalive_retry_count
flags.description: The maximum number of keepalive probes sent before declaring the client as dead. Effective only if --client_keepalive_probe_period_s is not 0.

flags.name: client_keepalive_retry_period_s
flags.description: The duration in second between successive keepalive probes from a client connection if the previous probes are not acknowledged. Effective only if --client_keepalive_probe_period_s is not 0.

flags.name: convert_legacy_hive_parquet_utc_timestamps
flags.description: When true, TIMESTAMPs read from files written by Parquet-MR (used by Hive) will be converted from UTC to local time. Writes are unaffected. Can be overriden with the query option with the same name.

flags.name: default_query_options
flags.description: key=value pair of default query options for impalad, separated by ','

flags.name: disconnected_session_timeout
flags.description: The time, in seconds, that a hiveserver2 session will be maintained after the last connection that it has been used over is disconnected.

flags.name: enable_external_fe_http
flags.description: if true enables http transport for external_fe_port otherwise binary transport is used

flags.name: executor_groups
flags.description: List of executor groups, separated by comma. Each executor group specification can optionally contain a minimum size, separated by a ':', e.g. --executor_groups default-pool-1:3. Default minimum size is 1. Only when the cluster membership contains at least that number of executors for the group will it be considered healthy for admission. Currently only a single group may be specified.

flags.name: expected_executor_group_sets
flags.description: Only used by the coordinator. List of expected executor group sets, separated by comma in the following format: <executor_group_name_prefix>:<expected_group_size> . For eg. “prefix1:10”, this set will include executor groups named like prefix1-group1, prefix1-group2, etc. The expected group size (number of executors in each group) is used during planning when no healthy executor group is available. If this flag is used then any executor groups that do not map to the specified group sets will never be used to schedule queries.

flags.name: external_fe_port
flags.description: port on which External Frontend requests are served. If 0 or less, the External Frontend server is not started. Careful consideration must be taken when enabling due to the fact that this port is currently always unauthenticated.

flags.name: fe_service_threads
flags.description: number of threads available to serve client requests

flags.name: hs2_http_port
flags.description: port on which HiveServer2 HTTP(s) client requests are served. If 0 or less, the HiveServer2 http server is not started.

flags.name: hs2_port
flags.description: port on which HiveServer2 client requests are served.If 0 or less, the HiveServer2 server is not started.

flags.name: idle_client_poll_period_s
flags.description: The poll period, in seconds, after no activity from an Impala client which an Impala service thread (beeswax and HS2) wakes up to check if the connection should be closed. If --idle_session_timeout is also set, a client connection will be closed if all the sessions associated with it have become idle. Set this to 0 to disable the polling behavior and clients' connection will remain opened until they are explicitly closed.

flags.name: idle_query_timeout
flags.description: The time, in seconds, that a query may be idle for (i.e. no processing work is done and no updates are received from the client) before it is cancelled. If 0, idle queries are never expired. The query option QUERY_TIMEOUT_S overrides this setting, but, if set, --idle_query_timeout represents the maximum allowable timeout.

flags.name: idle_session_timeout
flags.description: The time, in seconds, that a session may be idle for before it is closed (and all running queries cancelled) by Impala. If 0, idle sessions are never expired. It can be overridden by the query option 'idle_session_timeout' for specific sessions

flags.name: is_coordinator
flags.description: If true, this Impala daemon can accept and coordinate queries from clients. If false, it will refuse client connections.

flags.name: is_executor
flags.description: If true, this Impala daemon will execute query fragments.

flags.name: lineage_event_log_dir
flags.description: The directory in which lineage event log files are written. Setting this flag with enable lineage logging.

flags.name: log_query_to_file
flags.description: if true, logs completed query profiles to file.

flags.name: max_audit_event_log_file_size
flags.description: The maximum size (in queries) of the audit event log file before a new one is created (if event logging is enabled)

flags.name: max_audit_event_log_files
flags.description: Maximum number of audit event log files to retain. The most recent audit event log files are retained. If set to 0, all audit event log files are retained.

flags.name: max_hs2_sessions_per_user
flags.description: The maximum allowed number of HiveServer2 sessions that can be opened by any single connected user on a coordinator. If set to -1 or 0 then this check is not performed. If set to a positive value then the per-user session count is viewable in the webui under /sessions.

flags.name: max_lineage_log_file_size
flags.description: The maximum size (in queries) of the lineage event log file before a new one is created (if lineage logging is enabled)

flags.name: max_profile_log_file_size
flags.description: The maximum size (in queries) of the profile log file before a new one is created

flags.name: max_profile_log_files
flags.description: Maximum number of profile log files to retain. The most recent log files are retained. If set to 0, all log files are retained.

flags.name: max_result_cache_size
flags.description: Maximum number of query results a client may request to be cached on a per-query basis to support restarting fetches. This option guards against unreasonably large result caches requested by clients. Requests exceeding this maximum will be rejected.

flags.name: num_expected_executors
flags.description: The number of executors that are expected to be available for the execution of a single query. This value is used during planning if no executors have started yet. Once a healthy executor group has started, its size is used instead. NOTE: This flag is overridden by 'expected_executor_group_sets' which is a more expressive way of specifying multiple executor group sets

flags.name: profile_log_dir
flags.description: The directory in which profile log files are written. If blank, defaults to <log_file_dir>/profiles

flags.name: query_event_hook_classes
flags.description: Comma-separated list of java QueryEventHook implementation classes to load and register at Impala startup. Class names should be fully-qualified and on the classpath. Whitespace acceptable around delimiters.

flags.name: query_event_hook_nthreads
flags.description: Number of threads to use for QueryEventHook execution. If this number is >1 then hooks will execute concurrently.

flags.name: query_log_size
flags.description: Number of queries to retain in the query log. If -1, the query log has unbounded size. Used in combination with query_log_size_in_bytes, whichever is less.

flags.name: query_log_size_in_bytes
flags.description: Total maximum bytes of queries to retain in the query log. If -1, the query log has unbounded size. Used in combination with query_log_size, whichever is less

flags.name: query_stmt_size
flags.description: length of the statements in the query log. If <=0, the full statement is displayed in the query log without trimming.

flags.name: shutdown_deadline_s
flags.description: Default time limit in seconds for the shut down process. If this duration elapses after the shut down process is started, the daemon shuts down regardless of any running queries.

flags.name: shutdown_grace_period_s
flags.description: Shutdown startup grace period in seconds. When the shutdown process is started for this daemon, it will wait for at least the startup grace period before shutting down. This gives time for updated cluster membership information to propagate to all coordinators and for fragment instances that were scheduled based on old cluster membership to start executing (and therefore be reflected in the metrics used to detect quiescence).

flags.name: slow_profile_dump_warning_threshold_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Threshold for considering dumping a profile to be unusually slow.

flags.name: ssl_cipher_list
flags.description: The cipher suite preferences to use for TLS-secured Thrift RPC connections. Uses the OpenSSL cipher preference list format. See man (1) ciphers for more information. If empty, the default cipher list for your platform is used

flags.name: ssl_client_ca_certificate
flags.description: (Advanced) The full path to a certificate used by Thrift clients to check the validity of a server certificate. May either be a certificate for a third-party Certificate Authority, or a copy of the certificate the client expects to receive from the server.

flags.name: ssl_minimum_version
flags.description: The minimum SSL/TLS version that Thrift services should use for both client and server connections. Supported versions are TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2 (as long as the system OpenSSL library supports them)

flags.name: ssl_private_key
flags.description: The full path to the private key used as a counterpart to the public key contained in --ssl_server_certificate. If --ssl_server_certificate is set, this option must be set as well.

flags.name: ssl_private_key_password_cmd
flags.description: A Unix command whose output returns the password used to decrypt the certificate private key file specified in --ssl_private_key. If the .PEM key file is not password-protected, this command will not be invoked. The output of the command will be truncated to 1024 bytes, and then all trailing whitespace will be trimmed before it is used to decrypt the private key

flags.name: ssl_server_certificate
flags.description: The full path to the SSL certificate file used to authenticate Impala to clients. If set, both Beeswax and HiveServer2 ports will only accept SSL connections

flags.name: status_report_cancellation_padding
flags.description: (Advanced) The coordinator will wait --status_report_max_retry_s * (1 + --status_report_cancellation_padding / 100) without receiving a status report before deciding that a backend is unresponsive and the query should be cancelled. This must be > 0.

flags.name: status_report_interval_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Interval between profile reports in milliseconds. If set to <= 0, periodic reporting is disabled and only the final report is sent.

flags.name: status_report_max_retry_s
flags.description: (Advanced) Max amount of time in seconds for a backend to attempt to send a status report before cancelling. This must be > --status_report_interval_ms. Effective only if --status_report_interval_ms > 0.

flags.name: tls_ciphersuites
flags.description: The TLSv1.3 cipher suites to use for TLS-secured Thrift RPC and KRPC connections. TLSv1.3 uses a new way to specify ciper suites that is independent of the older TLSv1.2 and below cipher lists. See 'man (1) ciphers' for more information. This flag is only effective if Impala is built with OpenSSL v1.1.1 or newer.

flags.name: unregistration_thread_pool_queue_depth
flags.description: (Advanced) Max number of queries that can be queued for unregistration.

flags.name: unregistration_thread_pool_size
flags.description: (Advanced) Size of the thread-pool for unregistering queries, including finalizing runtime profiles

flags.name: use_local_tz_for_unix_timestamp_conversions
flags.description: When true, TIMESTAMPs are interpreted in the local time zone when converting to and from Unix times. When false, TIMESTAMPs are interpreted in the UTC time zone. Set to true for Hive compatibility. Can be overriden with the query option with the same name.

flags.name: wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_max_iterations
flags.description: This flag is used in the same situation as described at the '--wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_timeout_sec' flag. Instead of limiting the waiting time, the effect of this flag is that the coordinator gives up waiting after receiving the set number of valid catalog updates that do not change the catalog service ID. Negative values and zero have no effect. If both this flag and '--wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_timeout_sec' are set, the coordinator stops waiting when the stop condition of either of them is met. Note that it is possible that the coordinator does not receive any catalog update from the statestore and in this case it will wait indefinitely if '--wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_timeout_sec' is not set.

flags.name: wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_timeout_sec
flags.description: During DDL/DML queries, if there is a mismatch between the catalog service ID thatthe coordinator knows of and the one in the RPC response from the catalogd, the coordinator waits for a statestore update with a new catalog service ID in order to catch up with the one in the RPC response. However, in rare cases the service ID the coordinator knows of is the more recent one, in which case it could wait infinitely - to avoid this, this flag can be set to a positive value (in seconds) to limit the waiting time. Negative values and zero have no effect. See also '--wait_for_new_catalog_service_id_max_iterations,'.

flags.name: statestore_client_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for a catalog client RPC.

flags.name: statestore_subscriber_cnxn_attempts
flags.description: The number of times to retry an RPC connection to the statestore. A setting of 0 means retry indefinitely

flags.name: statestore_subscriber_cnxn_retry_interval_ms
flags.description: The interval, in ms, to wait between attempts to make an RPC connection to the statestore.

flags.name: statestore_subscriber_timeout_seconds
flags.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that may elapse before the connection with the statestore is considered lost.

flags.name: statestore_subscriber_use_resolved_address
flags.description: If set to true, the subscriber will register with statestore using its resolved IP address. Note that using resolved IP address may cause mismatch with the TLS certificate.

flags.name: enable_statestored_ha
flags.description: Set to true to enable Statestore HA

flags.name: state_store_peer_ha_port
flags.description: port where peer's StatestoreHaService is running

flags.name: state_store_peer_host
flags.description: hostname where peer's StatestoreHaService is running

flags.name: statestore_force_active
flags.description: Set to true to force this statestored instance to take active role. It's used to perform manual fail over for statestore service.

flags.name: statestore_ha_client_rpc_conn_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket conn timeout in milliseconds for a client RPC of Statestore HA service.

flags.name: statestore_ha_client_rpc_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for a client RPC of Statestore HA service.

flags.name: statestore_ha_preemption_wait_period_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which statestored designates itself as active role if the statestore does not receive HA handshake request/response from peer statestored.

flags.name: statestore_heartbeat_frequency_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Frequency (in ms) with which the statestore sends heartbeat heartbeats to subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_heartbeat_tcp_timeout_seconds
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which a heartbeat RPC to a subscriber will timeout. This setting protects against badly hung machines that are not able to respond to the heartbeat RPC in short order

flags.name: statestore_max_missed_heartbeats
flags.description: Maximum number of consecutive heartbeat messages an impalad can miss before being declared failed by the statestore.

flags.name: statestore_max_subscribers
flags.description: Used to control the maximum size of the pending topic-update queue. There is at most one entry per subscriber.

flags.name: statestore_num_heartbeat_threads
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of threads used to  send heartbeats in parallel to all registered subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_num_priority_update_threads
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of threads used to send prioritized topic updates in parallel to all registered subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_num_update_threads
flags.description: (Advanced) Number of threads used to  send topic updates in parallel to all registered subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_peer_cnxn_attempts
flags.description: The number of times to retry an RPC connection to the peer statestore. A setting of 0 means retry indefinitely

flags.name: statestore_peer_cnxn_retry_interval_ms
flags.description: The interval, in ms, to wait between attempts to make an RPC connection to the peer statestore. It's set as statestore_ha_preemption_wait_period_ms/statestore_peer_cnxn_attempts if statestore_peer_cnxn_attempts > 0, default value if statestore_peer_cnxn_attempts == 0.

flags.name: statestore_peer_timeout_seconds
flags.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that may elapse before the connection with the peer statestore is considered lost.

flags.name: statestore_priority_update_frequency_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Frequency (in ms) with which the statestore sends prioritized topic updates to subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_update_catalogd_tcp_timeout_seconds
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which a UpdateCatalogd RPC to a subscriber will timeout. This setting protects against badly hung machines that are not able to respond to the UpdateCatalogd RPC in short order

flags.name: statestore_update_frequency_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Frequency (in ms) with which the statestore sends topic updates to subscribers.

flags.name: statestore_update_statestore_tcp_timeout_seconds
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which a UpdateStatestoredRole RPC to a subscriber will timeout. This setting protects against badly hung machines that are not able to respond to the UpdateStatestoredRole RPC in short order.

flags.name: statestore_update_tcp_timeout_seconds
flags.description: (Advanced) The time after which an update RPC to a subscriber will timeout. This setting protects against badly hung machines that are not able to respond to the update RPC in short order.

flags.name: update_statestore_rpc_resend_interval_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Interval (in ms) with which the statestore resends the RPCs of updating statestored's role to subscribers if the statestore has failed to send the RPCs to the subscribers.

flags.name: use_network_address_as_statestore_priority
flags.description: Network address is used as priority value of statestored instance if this is set as true. Otherwise, statestored_id which is generated as random number will be used as priority value of statestored instance.

flags.name: force_lowercase_usernames
flags.description: If true, all principals and usernames are mapped to lowercase shortnames before being passed to any components (Ranger, admission control) for authorization

flags.name: sasl_connect_tcp_timeout_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) The underlying TSocket send/recv timeout in milliseconds for the initial SASL handeshake.

flags.name: allow_ordinals_in_having
flags.description: If true, allow using ordinals in HAVING clause. This non-standard feature is supported in Impala 3.x and earlier. We intend to disable it since 4.0. So it defaults to be false. See IMPALA-7844.

flags.name: avro_schema_url_allowed_schemes
flags.description: Comma-separated list of URI schemes permitted for avro.schema.url when loading schemas from a remote location. HTTP is never allowed via this setting. A URI with no scheme is resolved against the default filesystem.

flags.name: avro_schema_url_http_allowed_hosts
flags.description: Comma-separated list of hosts permitted for avro.schema.url when avro_schema_url_remote_http_enabled is true. HTTP schema fetch is rejected when this list is empty.

flags.name: avro_schema_url_remote_http_enabled
flags.description: Whether to allow avro.schema.url values that use http. When enabled, the host must also appear in avro_schema_url_http_allowed_hosts. Disabled by default to prevent server-side request forgery.

flags.name: enable_column_masking
flags.description: If false, disable the column masking feature. Defaults to be true.

flags.name: enable_row_filtering
flags.description: If false, disable the row filtering feature. Defaults to be true. Enabling this flag requires enable_column_masking to be true.

flags.name: ignored_dir_prefix_list
flags.description: Comma separated list to specify the prefix for tmp/staging dirs that catalogd should skip in loading file metadata.

flags.name: saml2_callback_token_ttl
flags.description: Time (in milliseconds) for which the token issued by service provider is valid.

flags.name: saml2_group_attribute_name
flags.description: The attribute name in the SAML assertion which would be used to compare for the group name matching. By default it is empty which would allow any authenticated user. If this value is set then saml2_group_filter must be set to a non-empty value.

flags.name: saml2_group_filter
flags.description: Comma separated list of group names which will be allowed when SAML authentication is enabled.

flags.name: saml2_idp_metadata
flags.description: IDP metadata file for the SAML configuration. This metadata file must be exported from the external identity provider. This is used to validate the SAML assertions received. Setting this is required for SAML authentication

flags.name: saml2_keystore_password_cmd
flags.description: Command that outputs the password to the keystore used to sign the authentication requests. Setting this is required for SAML authentication.

flags.name: saml2_keystore_path
flags.description: Keystore path to the saml2 client. This keystore is used to store the key pair used to sign the authentication requests when saml2_sign_requests is set to true. If the path doesn't exist, HiveServer2 will attempt to create a keystore using the default configurations otherwise it will use the one provided. Setting this is required for SAML authentication.

flags.name: saml2_private_key_password_cmd
flags.description: Command that outputs the password for the private key which is stored in the keystore pointed by saml2_keystore_path. This key is used to sign the authentication request if saml2_sign_requests is set to true.

flags.name: saml2_sign_requests
flags.description: When this configuration is set to true, Impala will sign the SAML requests which can be validated by the IDP provider.

flags.name: saml2_sp_callback_url
flags.description: Callback URL where SAML responses should be posted. Currently this must be configured at the same port number as the --hs2_http_port flag.

flags.name: saml2_sp_entity_id
flags.description: Service provider entity id for this impalad. This must match with the SP id on the external identity provider. If this is not set, saml2_sp_callback_url will be used as the SP id.

flags.name: saml2_want_assertations_signed
flags.description: When this configuration is set to true, Impala will validate the signature of the assertions received at the callback url. 'False' should be only used for testing as it makes the protocol unsecure.

flags.name: startup_filesystem_check_directories
flags.description: Comma separated list of directories to list on startup to verify access to the filesystem. The default is to list the root of the filesytem. This can be specified to a subdirectory to avoid accesses to the root of the filesystem. To disable the startup check, specify the empty string.

flags.name: use_hms_column_order_for_hbase_tables
flags.description: Use the column order in HMS for HBase tables instead of ordering the columns by family/qualifier. Keeping the default as false for backward compatibility.

flags.name: warn_catalog_response_duration_s
flags.description: Threshold in seconds to log a warning for slow catalogd response.

flags.name: warn_catalog_response_size_mb
flags.description: Threshold in MB to log a warning for large catalogd response size.

flags.name: num_cores
flags.description: (Advanced) If > 0, it sets the number of cores available to Impala. Setting it to 0 means Impala will use all available cores on the machine according to /proc/cpuinfo.

flags.name: web_log_bytes
flags.description: The maximum number of bytes to display on the debug webserver's log page

flags.name: jvm_deadlock_detector_interval_s
flags.description: (Advanced) Interval between JVM deadlock checks. If set to 0 or a negative value, deadlock checks are disabled.

flags.name: ldap_group_search_basedn
flags.description: The 'distinguished name' DN that will be used to search for the authenticating group. If left empty, group checks will not be performed.

flags.name: ldap_user_search_basedn
flags.description: The 'distinguished name' DN that will be used to search for the authenticating user, this field is required for search bind authentication.

flags.name: ldap_baseDN
flags.description: If set, Impala will try to bind to LDAP with a name of the form uid=<userid>,<ldap_baseDN>

flags.name: ldap_bind_pattern
flags.description: If set, Impala will try to bind to LDAP with a name of <ldap_bind_pattern>, but where the string #UID is replaced by the user ID. Use to control the bind name precisely; do not set --ldap_domain or --ldap_baseDN with this option

flags.name: ldap_domain
flags.description: If set, Impala will try to bind to LDAP with a name of the form <userid>@<ldap_domain>

flags.name: ldap_group_class_key
flags.description: The LDAP objectClass each of the groups in --ldap_group_filter implements in LDAP.

flags.name: ldap_group_dn_pattern
flags.description: Colon separated list of patterns for the 'distinguished name' used to search for groups in the directory. Each pattern may contain a '%s' which will be substituted with each group name from --ldap_group_filter when doing group searches.

flags.name: ldap_group_membership_key
flags.description: The LDAP attribute on group entries that indicates its members.

flags.name: allow_custom_ldap_filters_with_kerberos_auth
flags.description: If set, will allow custom LDAP user and group filters even if Kerberos authentication is enabled. Disabled by default.

flags.name: ldap_allow_anonymous_binds
flags.description: (Advanced) If true, LDAP authentication with a blank password (an 'anonymous bind') is allowed by Impala.

flags.name: ldap_bind_dn
flags.description: Distinguished name of the user to bind as when doing user or group searches. Only required if user or group filters are being used and the LDAP server is not configured to allow anonymous searches.

flags.name: ldap_bind_password_cmd
flags.description: A Unix command whose output returns the password to use with --ldap_bind_dn. The output of the command will be truncated to 1024 bytes and trimmed of trailing whitespace.

flags.name: ldap_passwords_in_clear_ok
flags.description: If set, will allow LDAP passwords to be sent in the clear (without TLS/SSL) over the network.  This option should not be used in production environments

flags.name: ldap_search_bind_authentication
flags.description: If set to true, LDAP search bind authentication will be used instead of the default simple bind.

flags.name: ldap_tls
flags.description: If true, use the secure TLS protocol to connect to the LDAP server

flags.name: ldap_uri
flags.description: The URI of the LDAP server to authenticate users against

flags.name: non_impala_java_vlog
flags.description: (Advanced) The log level (equivalent to --v) for non-Impala Java classes (0: INFO, 1 and 2: DEBUG, 3: TRACE)

flags.name: disable_parquetbloomfilter_avx2
flags.description: Disable AVX2 operations in ParquetBloomFilter. This flag has no effect if the target CPU doesn't support AVX2 at run-time or ParquetBloomFilter was built with a compiler that doesn't support AVX2.

flags.name: periodic_counter_update_period_ms
flags.description: Period to update query profile rate counters and sampling counters in ms

flags.name: periodic_system_counter_update_period_ms
flags.description: Period to update system-level rate counters and sampling counters in ms

flags.name: disable_content_security_policy_header
flags.description: If true then the webserver will not add the Content-Security-Policy HTTP header to HTTP responses

flags.name: enable_webserver_doc_root
flags.description: If true, webserver may serve static files from the webserver_doc_root

flags.name: slow_http_response_warning_threshold_ms
flags.description: (Advanced) Threshold for considering a HTTP response to be unusually slow.

flags.name: webserver_authentication_domain
flags.description: Domain used for debug webserver authentication

flags.name: webserver_certificate_file
flags.description: The location of the debug webserver's SSL certificate file, in .pem format. If empty, webserver SSL support is not enabled

flags.name: webserver_doc_root
flags.description: Files under <webserver_doc_root>/www are accessible via the debug webserver. Defaults to $IMPALA_HOME, or if $IMPALA_HOME is not set, disables the document root

flags.name: webserver_interface
flags.description: Interface to start debug webserver on. If blank, webserver binds to 0.0.0.0

flags.name: webserver_ldap_group_filter
flags.description: Used as filter for both simple and search bind mechanisms for the webserver authentication. For simple bind it is a comma separated list of groups. If specified, users must belong to one of these groups for authentication to succeed. For search bind it is an LDAP filter that will be used during LDAP group search, it can contain '{0}' pattern which will be replaced with the user name and/or '{1}' which will be replace with the user dn.

flags.name: webserver_ldap_passwords_in_clear_ok
flags.description: (Advanced) If true, allows the webserver to start with LDAP authentication even if SSL is not enabled, a potentially insecure configuration.

flags.name: webserver_ldap_user_filter
flags.description: Used as filter for both simple and search bind mechanisms for the webserver authentication. For simple bind it is a comma separated list of user names. If specified, users must be on this list for authentication to succeed. For search bind it is an LDAP filter that will be used during LDAP search, it can contain '{0}' pattern which will be replaced with the user name.

flags.name: webserver_max_post_length_bytes
flags.description: The maximum length of a POST request that will be accepted by the embedded web server.

flags.name: webserver_password_file
flags.description: (Optional) Location of .htpasswd file containing user names and hashed passwords for debug webserver authentication. Cannot be used with --webserver_require_ldap or --webserver_require_spnego.

flags.name: webserver_port
flags.description: Port to start debug webserver on

flags.name: webserver_private_key_file
flags.description: The full path to the private key used as a counterpart to the public key contained in --webserver_certificate_file. If --webserver_certificate_file is set, this option must be set as well.

flags.name: webserver_private_key_password_cmd
flags.description: A Unix command whose output returns the password used to decrypt the Webserver's certificate private key file specified in --webserver_private_key_file. If the .PEM key file is not password-protected, this command will not be invoked. The output of the command will be truncated to 1024 bytes, and then all trailing whitespace will be trimmed before it is used to decrypt the private key

flags.name: webserver_require_ldap
flags.description: Require connections to the web server to authenticate via LDAP using HTTP Basic authentication. Cannot be used with --webserver_require_spnego or --webserver_password_file.

flags.name: webserver_require_spnego
flags.description: Require connections to the web server to authenticate via Kerberos using SPNEGO. Cannot be used with --webserver_require_ldap or --webserver_password_file.

flags.name: webserver_x_frame_options
flags.description: webserver will add X-Frame-Options HTTP header with this value

flags.name: cluster_id
flags.description: Specifies an identifier string that uniquely represents this cluster. This identifier is included in the query log table if enabled.

flags.name: enable_workload_mgmt
flags.description: Specifies if Impala will automatically write completed queries in the query log table. If this value is set to true and then later removed, the query log table will remain intact and accessible.

flags.name: query_log_max_plan_length
flags.description: Maximum length of the sql plan that will be recorded in the completed queries table. If a plan has a length longer than this value, the plan inserted into the completed queries table will be trimmed to this length. Any characters that need escaping will have their backslash character counted towards this limit.

flags.name: query_log_max_queued
flags.description: Maximum number of records that can be queued before they are written to the impala query log table. This flag operates independently of the 'query_log_write_interval_s' flag. If the number of queued records reaches this value, the records will be written to the query log table no matter how much time has passed since the last write. The countdown to the next write (based on the time period defined in the 'query_log_write_interval_s' flag) is not restarted.

flags.name: query_log_max_sql_length
flags.description: Maximum length of a sql statement that will be recorded in the completed queries table. If a sql statement with a length longer than this value is executed, the sql inserted into the completed queries table will be trimmed to this length. Any characters that need escaping will have their backslash character counted towards this limit.

flags.name: query_log_request_pool
flags.description: Specifies a pool or queue used by the queries that insert into the query log table. Empty value causes no pool to be set.

flags.name: query_log_write_interval_s
flags.description: Number of seconds to wait between batches of inserts to the query log table. The countdown to the next write starts immediately when a write begins, but a new write will not start until the prior write has completed. Min value is 1. Max value is 14400.

flags.name: alsologtoemail
flags.description: log messages go to these email addresses in addition to logfiles

flags.name: alsologtostderr
flags.description: log messages go to stderr in addition to logfiles

flags.name: colorlogtostderr
flags.description: color messages logged to stderr (if supported by terminal)

flags.name: drop_log_memory
flags.description: Drop in-memory buffers of log contents. Logs can grow very quickly and they are rarely read before they need to be evicted from memory. Instead, drop them from memory as soon as they are flushed to disk.

flags.name: log_backtrace_at
flags.description: Emit a backtrace when logging at file:linenum.

flags.name: log_dir
flags.description: If specified, logfiles are written into this directory instead of the default logging directory.

flags.name: log_link
flags.description: Put additional links to the log files in this directory

flags.name: log_prefix
flags.description: Prepend the log prefix to the start of each log line

flags.name: logbuflevel
flags.description: Buffer log messages logged at this level or lower (-1 means don't buffer; 0 means buffer INFO only; ...)

flags.name: logbufsecs
flags.description: Buffer log messages for at most this many seconds

flags.name: logemaillevel
flags.description: Email log messages logged at this level or higher (0 means email all; 3 means email FATAL only; ...)

flags.name: logfile_mode
flags.description: Log file mode/permissions.

flags.name: logmailer
flags.description: Mailer used to send logging email

flags.name: logtostderr
flags.description: log messages go to stderr instead of logfiles

flags.name: max_log_size
flags.description: approx. maximum log file size (in MB). A value of 0 will be silently overridden to 1.

flags.name: minloglevel
flags.description: Messages logged at a lower level than this don't actually get logged anywhere

flags.name: stderrthreshold
flags.description: log messages at or above this level are copied to stderr in addition to logfiles.  This flag obsoletes --alsologtostderr.

flags.name: stop_logging_if_full_disk
flags.description: Stop attempting to log to disk if the disk is full.

flags.name: symbolize_stacktrace
flags.description: Symbolize the stack trace in the tombstone

flags.name: v
flags.description: Show all VLOG(m) messages for m <= this. Overridable by --vmodule.

flags.name: vmodule
flags.description: per-module verbose level. Argument is a comma-separated list of <module name>=<log level>. <module name> is a glob pattern, matched against the filename base (that is, name ignoring .cc/.h./-inl.h). <log level> overrides any value given by --v.
